FIP.thesis_summary: A signed $1.52 billion sale of the Long Ridge power plant to MARA, awaiting only a change-of-control approval from the energy regulator, guided to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026 and cutting total debt from $3.8 billion to $2.4 billion; the shares at $4.23 sit near their fifty-two-week low against a $9.00 event-resolved value and a realistic $2.75 deal-break price.
FIP.dated_milestone: Change-of-control approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, application filed 8 May 2026 in docket EC26-92, guided by management to arrive in the middle of the third quarter of 2026, with the sale closing by 30 September 2026 on the seller's guidance. Nearest scheduled checkpoint: second-quarter 2026 results after the close on Wednesday 5 August 2026, with the conference call at 8:00 a.m. Eastern on Thursday 6 August 2026.
FIP.kill_risk: [CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTIONS] The '14x private-market mark' that anchors the entire sum-of-the-parts is not what the buyer says it paid. The bull derives 14x by annualising Long Ridge's outage-impacted Q1-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $26.4m ($105.6m) against the $1.512bn base price. MARA's own 30 April 2026 announcement states Long Ridge contributes approximately $144 million of annualised adjusted EBITDA (second-half 2025 basis, reflecting the February 2025 hedge swaps and the June 2025 capacity payments) - i.e. the buyer underwrote roughly 10.5x, not 14x. That number is load-bearing in three place

FIP.dossier_note: Buy it now, and size it as a levered stub with a live event rather than as an arbitrage with a floor. The event is genuine. A definitive agreement was signed on 29 April 2026 to sell the Long Ridge power plant to MARA for about $1.52 billion, the regulatory application was filed on 8 May in docket EC26-92, the buyer cleared its bondholder consents in June, no financing contingency exists, and management has guided to approval by the middle of the third quarter. Nothing about it has fired, and the shares have actually fallen since the announcement, so none of the re-rating has been spent. At $4.23, close to the fifty-two-week low of $3.90 and against a high of $7.94, you are being paid to wait for a transaction that reduces total debt from $3.8 billion to $2.4 billion and saves about $30 million of interest a year, on a company whose surviving railroads grew earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation 31% year over year. There is no wash-out worth waiting for; this is the wash-out. Two things keep this from being the maximum-conviction version of this setup. The first is the floor. The entry carried into this review assumes $3.90 of downside protection, and that number is a chart level, not a recovery value. Book equity is negative $303.1 million, there is no net cash, operating cash flow was negative $69.4 million last quarter, and the filing's own liquidity assurance is expressly conditioned on this sale closing. A deal-break realistically prices the shares

VRDN.thesis_summary: The catalyst has already fired: the FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) for thyroid eye disease on 26 June 2026, four days ahead of its 30 June target date and with a broader label than expected - and the stock is at $19.70 a month later, so the re-rating we were waiting to be paid for has been spent without paying, leaving roughly 52% upside to a $30 good-launch value against 57% downside to an $8.50 cash-based floor.
VRDN.dated_milestone: FDA approval granted 26 June 2026 (the target decision date was 30 June 2026) - fired, favourably and early, with the launch beginning the same week. Remaining calendar, none of it hard or binding: second-quarter results expected around 5 August 2026 (a stub month of launch revenue); management's guidance of broad insurance coverage within six to nine months of launch, pointing to roughly December 2026 through March 2027; a company-controlled approval filing for elegrobart targeted for the first quarter of 2027; and a European decision expected during 2027 on the application accepted in February 2026.
VRDN.kill_risk: [REFUTED] The catalyst has fired and nothing dated, binding or agency-controlled replaces it. Verified against the company's own 26 June 2026 release: the FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) 'for the treatment of thyroid eye disease regardless of thyroid eye disease activity or duration', four days ahead of the 30 June 2026 PDUFA target action date, with no advisory committee, no complete response letter, and immediate launch -- physicians 'can prescribe Lumvoa tomorrow'. That is the best available version of the event this sleeve underwrote, and the tape refused it: the live quote is $19.70

VRDN.dossier_note:
This is a pass for now, and the reason is simple enough to state in one sentence: we were underwriting a dated regulatory decision, that decision arrived on 26 June 2026 - early, clean, and with a broader label than we expected - and the stock is at $19.70 a month later. When the best available outcome of a binary event does not pay, the market is pricing something the event did not address, and continuing to hold is no longer the trade we sized. It is a different trade wearing the old trade's clothes.

What the market is pricing is the 30 March 2026 data on elegrobart, the under-the-skin follow-on. That trial met its goal but at roughly 36 to 45 placebo-adjusted percentage points against about 64 for the approved infused drug, and the shares fell roughly a third that day and never recovered. The self-administered format is what was supposed to carry a chronic-disease franchise over a decade. A weaker version of it is a smaller company, and an approval for the infused drug does not repair that.

Two corrections to our own file, pulling in opposite directions. First, the balance sheet is much stronger than we carried: the company raised $350 million gross in May 2026 - shares at $17.00 plus 1.75% notes due 2032 - and collected a $75 million approval milestone from its royalty partner in late June, so cash is roughly $1.0 billion, not $600 million. The dilution risk we flagged as the way the floor breaks has already been taken, before the event, which is good treasury disciplin

EYPT.thesis_summary: The underwritten catalyst is spent. EyePoint's LUGANO pivotal Phase 3 — the readout the board dated to 2026-07-31 — fired on 2026-08-17 and MISSED its prespecified primary endpoint (change from baseline in BCVA vs on-label 2mg aflibercept) in the full randomized dataset. Non-inferiority appears only in an analysis the company itself labels ad hoc, excluding 9 of 211 DURAVYU patients (4%) who lost 15+ letters, against ZERO comparable cases in the control arm; the attached p=0.0096 is nominal and carries no regulatory weight. The tape resolved on the loss leg: $14.75 (2026-08-14) to $4.87 (2026-08-25 close, FMP), about -67%, with the 52-week low of $3.95 set the same week — i.e. BELOW the board's claimed $5.50 "floor," which was an assertion rather than an asset. The board's $37.50 target was RBC's pre-readout number; RBC withdrew it on 2026-08-18, cutting to $5 and downgrading to Sector Perform (Chardan $65 to $5, Jefferies $30 to $8, Jones $43 to $20, Citi to $17, JPMorgan to Neutral). A successor exists but is NOT the event we owned: LUCIA, the second identically designed pivotal, is fully enrolled with topline guided by the company to "the fourth quarter of 2026" (press reporting narrows it to October, not a company-fixed date), with an NDA in 1H 2027 contingent on it. That is a fresh, undated, unhedged binary in front of a near-certain financing — not the resolution of the dated event this seat was underwritten on.
EYPT.kill_risk: My load-bearing claim is that the edge is spent because LUGANO fired and failed and the successor is undated. Two credible refutations survive. (1) TIMING: the company's WRITTEN guidance is "Q4 2026," but sell-side and trade press since 2026-08-17 report LUCIA topline "expected in October." If EyePoint firms that into a fixed date, a re-underwritable dated binary sets up roughly six weeks after a FIRED exit — the classic sell-the-wreck-then-watch-it-double failure mode, and from a $4.87 base with ~$180m of cash behind it the win leg is a multiple, not a spread. My status is correct on today's record but has a short shelf life; re-poll before the sleeve treats this name as permanently dead. (2) VALUATION DIRECTION: at $408m cap against $180.5m cash and no borrowed debt, roughly $228m of program value is still priced in — this is NOT a max-fear print, so the risk to my $1.75 lose-leg is that it is far below where the tape would actually clear, while my 0.30 win_prob may itself be generous given XBI near a five-year high makes market-implied probabilities structurally rich. Residual risk cuts both ways: the floor is too low for a tactical mark and the entry is not cheap enough for a fresh binary.

EYPT.dossier_note:
FIRED, verified three ways. EyePoint's 2026-08-17 release (globenewswire + investors.eyepoint.bio; 8-K accession 0001193125-26-353308), Reuters 2026-08-17 ("EyePoint's eye drug misses main goal in late-stage trial"), and the tape ($14.75 on 08-14 to $4.87 on 08-25, -67%) all agree: LUGANO did not meet the prespecified primary. The board's date (2026-07-31) was already wrong pre-fire by 17 days.

WHY THE $37.50 CANNOT BE REPRODUCED. It was RBC's pre-readout target, withdrawn 2026-08-18 (cut to $5, downgrade to Sector Perform). Same-day broker resets: Chardan $65->$5, Jefferies $30->$8, Jones $43->$20, Citi ->$17, JPMorgan ->Neutral (pre-miss Street average was $38.58). The board's target had no independent derivation behind it — it was a single withdrawn sell-side print.

WIN LEG = $17.00 (LUCIA-conditional, NOT a mark on the fired event). The surviving post-cut targets ($5/$5/$8/$17/$20) are blended numbers that already carry LUCIA risk; a clean LUCIA primary win should clear the top of that band but stays far below $37.50 because one-win/one-miss on the prespecified endpoint is a materially weaker NDA than two wins, and the July-2024 cGMP Warning Letter on the Watertown YUTIQ line sits on the CMC path for a company whose only asset is a manufactured drug-eluting insert (nuance vs the board skeptic: the 10-Q states the required corrective and preventive action plan was FULLY EXECUTED, so this is an overhang, not a confirmed open deficiency). $17.00 = Citi's post-cut mark, below Jones' $20; deliberately taken as the conservative end.

LOSE LEG = $1.75, from the balance sheet, not assertion. 6/30/26 (10-Q filed 2026-08-05): cash + ST investments $180.472m, ZERO borrowed debt, $22.367m finance-lease obligations, payables + accrued $39.3m, equity $166.4m, 83.84m shares out. July ATM added ~1,208,718 shares (~$17m; corroborated — Q2 ATM was 1,429,047 sh at $14.16 wtd avg = $20.2m gross, matching Q2 cash-flow common stock issuance of $20.178m). Realized burn: Q1 op CF -$80.5m, Q2 -$62.3m = $142.9m in H1, roughly $71m/quarter. Carrying to a 12/31/26 readout: $180.5m + $17m - ~$105m (two tapering quarters) = ~$92m, less $22.4m leases = ~$70m net, over ~85m shares = ~$0.82/share of hard net cash. Adding residual DME optionality (COMO/CAPRI fully enrolled, 480+ patients, topline Q4 2027) and YUTIQ gets a busted-single-asset clearing price of $1.50-2.00; I take $1.75.

RUNWAY DISCREPANCY WORTH THE CRO'S ATTENTION. The company guides $180m as runway "into Q4 2027," which implies about $33m/quarter — less than HALF the realized H1 2026 rate of ~$71m/quarter. At the realized rate $180m is ~2.5 quarters (into roughly Q1 2027). The guided runway therefore requires a >50% spend taper or further ATM issuance, and the ATM is already routine — the next tranche prints near a third of the $14.16/$14.44 levels at which the last two were sold.

WIN_PROB 0.30. LUCIA is the same molecule, same insert, same comparator, same endpoint. The bull case is that LUGANO's miss was an artifact of 9 of 211 DURAVYU patients losing 15+ letters "unrelated to wet AMD." But 9/211 versus 0/211 in control is not a chance imbalance (Fisher exact approx. p=0.004 two-sided) — the likelier reading is drug- or device-related, which recurs in an identically designed trial. That is the single strongest reason 0.60 cannot carry over.

EV CHECK, for transparency only (sizing is the Director's): 0.30 x $17.00 + 0.70 x $1.75 = $5.10 + $1.23 = $6.33 against $4.87 spot. Positive on paper — but attached to an UNDATED event, unhedged, with a dilutive raise standing in front of it. catalyst_live=false is the operative field here; these axes exist so the seat is not adjudicated off a dead $37.50/$5.50 pair.

TAKEOUT LENS — NO LIFT APPLIED. The 2026 record-pace biotech M&A cohort (37 takeouts >=$1B YTD, $216B) is late-stage, commercially-ready assets; a failed prespecified primary disqualifies EYPT from that cohort today, so strategic scarcity is currently negative, not positive. The retina precedent that would frame a conditional bid is Astellas/Iveric Bio ($5.9B, April 2023) — but it is three years stale and was a clean pre-approval asset, so it does not carry provenance strong enough to lift the win leg, and I have not lifted it. Any takeout interest is contingent on a LUCIA win, is undated, and is explicitly NOT treated as a milestone.

REGIME CAVEAT. XBI near a five-year high means market-implied win probabilities are rich and old max-fear floor prints are stale-low. Cutting the other way: $408m cap on $180.5m cash means ~$228m of program value is STILL priced in post-crash, so this is not a capitulation print, and the gap between $4.87 and my $1.75 lose-leg is the honest measure of how much LUCIA optimism the tape is already carrying.

LZM.dated_milestone: One real calendar item and one real deadline, neither of which is the catalyst itself. (1) First-half 2026 interim financial results on 29 July 2026, with an investor webcast at 10:00 a.m. New York time hosted by chief executive Chris Showalter and chief financial officer Ingo Hofmaier -- confirmed by the company on 27 July 2026 and verified today. This is a disclosure venue at which management must either produce the concluded process or explain a second missed milestone; it resolves nothing by itself. (2) The Taurus senior secured bridge matures on 31 July 2027, which is the outer bound on how long this can drift -- a deadline that works for the lender, not the shareholder. The catalyst proper -- the strategic-partner transaction -- has no announced date, and the two gates behind it, the Framework Agreement amendment with the Tanzanian government and the power supply agreements, are undated as well.

LZM.dossier_note:
This is a real event on a broken clock, and the discipline that makes this funnel work is the discipline to say so.

Start with what is true. Kabanga is a genuine tier-one orebody -- among the largest and highest-grade development-ready nickel sulfide deposits anywhere, in the cheapest quarter of the cost curve, with an independently prepared study value of $1.58 billion against a $298 million company. The sale process is real, competitive and advanced, corroborated by a wire-service leak specific enough that the company had to respond on 8 June 2026. If it concludes at a defensible fraction of study value, $7.00 is a defensible number and this roughly doubles.

Now what is not true. This is not a defined-risk event position, and treating it as one is the error the catalyst discipline exists to prevent. There is no date: the guided mid-2026 build decision lapsed silently, and 'concluding shortly' was said eighty-nine days ago. There is nothing binding: no agreement, no outside date, no regulator on a clock, no contractual payout. Two hard prerequisites -- a sovereign fiscal amendment and a utility power agreement -- are themselves undated, and one of them cannot be scheduled by anybody. And the floor our board carried at $2.60 is folklore. DDL.thesis_summary: Dingdong (Cayman) has a signed 5-Feb-2026 SPA to sell its China business to Two Hearts Investments Limited, a wholly owned Meituan subsidiary, for US$717m cash struck off the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet, on top of which the listed parent was permitted to draw up to US$280m of cash out of the China group pre-closing (the company's own "up to US$997m" framing). Shareholders approved both the SPA and the capital-return authority on 27 Mar 2026; there is no financing contingency. Verified live on 2026-09-08: the extraction is substantially done (US$267.1m of cash and short-term investments at the parent at 30 Jun 2026 versus RMB45.7m at 31 Dec 2025) and the deal is unfired — the most recent SEC filing of any type for CIK 0001854545 is the 21 Aug 2026 6-K, which still names SAMR anti-monopoly clearance as an outstanding closing condition. The trade is therefore not a dated arb but an undated capital-return claim on offshore cash: at US$2.26 (216.7m ADS, US$489m market cap) the tape prices roughly half of a ~US$984m gross claim, and the gap is regulatory-timing plus governance and PRC-tax leakage rather than deal-break risk alone.
DDL.kill_risk: Seven months and three days after signing there is still no public SAMR trace — no acceptance notice, no simplified-procedure publication, no decision — and searches of SAMR concentration case lists and of Meituan/Dingdong filings turn up nothing; for a platform-sector concentration that consolidates fresh instant retail under Meituan's Xiaoxiang, and against the January 2026 State Council antitrust review of food-delivery platforms in which Meituan was named, that silence is at least as consistent with an extended review as with a routine one. Second and independent: even on close, the cash reaching ADS holders is a permission rather than an obligation — AGM Resolution 2 authorises a return "at such time, in such manner as the Board, in its absolute discretion, deems appropriate" — while the consideration is expressly "subject to adjustments based on certain net cash, net working capital and other financial line items ... as of certain agreed upon dates" plus a leakage deduction, and 10% of it is payable only after the Company settles PRC taxes on the transaction, including the non-resident indirect-transfer filings that are themselves a closing condition. So both the amount and the arrival are contingent, and neither has a date attached.

DDL.dossier_note:
STATUS. Catalyst is real, idiosyncratic and unfired, but it is not dated. Verified 2026-09-08: FMP SEC-filing index for CIK 0001854545 returns exactly one filing since 1 Jun 2026, the 6-K of 21 Aug 2026, whose text still says the transaction "remains pending ... contingent on standard closing conditions ... notably anti-monopoly approval from SAMR." No press release since the 20 Aug 2026 Q2 results. No SAMR publication found in English or Chinese searches, and no Meituan or Dingdong statement of clearance. Nothing has closed, no buyback and no dividend has been declared, and the spread has not moved (US$2.26, flat).

CALENDAR, corrected. (i) 31 Aug 2026 — the contractual window to pull up to US$280m of cash to the listed parent: PASSED and substantially met. Parent-level cash plus short-term investments at 30 Jun 2026 is RMB1,421.2m + RMB391.3m = RMB1,812.5m = US$267.1m, against RMB45.7m at 31 Dec 2025. The residual ~US$13m of allowance (about six cents an ADS) is permanently forgone; the company has published no final drawn figure. (ii) ~Nov 2026 — Q3 results, the next scheduled disclosure of any kind, not binding. (iii) 5 Feb 2027 — the twelve-month long-stop, extendable by mutual consent, which the buyer has every incentive to extend because post-signing target profits accrue to it. WIN LEG, arithmetic (216.7m ADS, from the filed Q2-2026 diluted count of 324,989,883 ordinary at 2 ADS per 3 ordinary; cross-checks to the quoted US$489.4m market cap at US$2.26 — the board's stale 224.6m ADS count overstates the divisor). The trade is the holdco discount closing: on management's own Q2 marks, guided year-end corporate cash of ~$2.0bn ($5.87/sh) plus the Liberty Growth portfolio at $2.9bn FMV ($8.50/sh) equals $14.37/sh with every telecom asset — 90% of Ziggo Group, 50% of Virgin Media O2, VM Ireland — carried at zero. The listing is the mechanism that forces the market to mark the telecom stub, exactly as the 2024 Sunrise spin did. It is genuinely idiosyncratic: nothing about the outcome depends on the tape, only on whether Liberty Global executes a distribution it has already restructured itself to make. What it is NOT is dated. There is no record date, no listing prospectus, no scheduled shareholder vote; guidance was tightened to "as early as mid-2027" in the 24 July Q2 release and then restated as plain "2027" in the 3 August completion release, and the board retains the right to abandon.

The EUR1.0bn (~$1.15bn) Vodafone payment went out on 3 August, leaving roughly $0.46bn of corporate cash plus $76m of separately-managed-account investments. Getting to $2.0bn by 31 December therefore needs ~$1.5bn of further H2 inflows, and the disposals named to supply it — the 50% Wyre stake (guided only to year-end 2026 or Q1 2027), the VodafoneZiggo towers, Belgian and Dutch property, EUR1.2-1.4bn in total — are described in the company's own 3 August release as proceeds that "will be used to retire debt" at the subsidiaries, not upstreamed to the holding company. LBTYK.dossier_note:

The 3 August 2026 completion of the VodafoneZiggo buyout (EUR1.0bn cash + 10% stake to Vodafone; Liberty Global at 90%) removes the last structural contingency: no JV partner, no pending approval, no financing condition. It is also not a slip - the dossier expected close "by 31 July", it landed 3 August. Not FIRED, because the buyout is preparatory; the resolving event is the distribution and Euronext Amsterdam listing of Ziggo Group, which has not happened. PENDING_SOFT rather than PENDING_HARD because nothing binds the date: the 24 July Q2 release said "the planned Ziggo Group spin-off as early as mid-2027", the 3 August release says only "list Ziggo Group in Amsterdam in 2027", and there is no record date, no prospectus and no scheduled vote. (1) Guided stack, which is where the board's $18 lives. This reconciles to management's own Q2 statement that cash plus growth marks exceed the share price by about 30% ($4.9bn vs $3.63bn = +35%). The board's $18 implies $6.14bn, i.e. $1.24bn or $3.64/sh for the entire telecom portfolio - roughly 0.2x revenue for the Ziggo equity alone against EUR6.6bn of revenue and ~EUR2.5bn of combined EBITDA. On that basis $18 is reproducible and, if anything, undemanding, so I keep it.

(2) Hard marks today, which the board number quietly assumes away. Corporate-level liquidity was $1,610.1m at 30 June (the 10-Q is explicit that only this slice is available at the corporate level; $808.5m of the $2,418.6m consolidated sits trapped in the Telenet and VM Ireland borrowing groups, and Liberty Global standalone held $0). No marketing application is on file, so no regulator-set decision date exists; the actual binary (approval) is mid-2027 at the earliest on priority review, late 2027 on standard. (2) The EV sign is also not robust to branch structure: on the skeptic's four-outcome weights (22/33/30/15) the same corrected axes produce roughly $10 per ADS, below the price. (3) Structural dilution drag: the $150M ATM was refreshed July 17, 2026 and $50M was already drawn to RA Capital on July 30 at a filing that has since not happened. DBVT.dossier_note:
CATALYST REALITY. Verified unfired and forward-dated, but soft and company-controlled, and it has already slipped once. Primary chain: March 2025 guidance = filing in 1H 2026 (missed); June 29, 2026 8-K re-guided to Q3 2026 after iterative FDA engagement confined to organization, mapping and formatting of existing CMC and biostatistics data sets, with the agency explicitly requesting no additional data; July 16, 2026 Q2 release restated Q3 2026 and reported $174.9M cash at June 30 funding into Q3 2027; September 3, 2026 conference release still describes the company as late-stage with the filing pending. DBV's EDGAR index shows no 8-K after July 16, 2026, so no submission has been announced as of September 8, 2026 with 22 days left in the window. Status = SLIPPED (1H 2026 -> Q3 2026). One caveat I could not fully settle: a secondary web result referenced a Q4 2026 submission after an FDA alignment meeting, but no primary source — no 8-K, no press release, no Euronext filing — supports it, and every primary document says Q3 2026. I did not adopt it; treat a Q4 restatement as a live risk to be checked at the Cantor (Sept 9), Citi (Sept 10) or H.C. Wainwright (Sept 15) fireside chats, any of which could re-guide.

WHY THE DRIVER TAG CHANGED. The catalyst the board is priced against — the VITESSE readout — fired on December 16, 2025 and its re-rating is spent. Tagging this FDA_clinical_readout puts a name whose readout is behind it into the same deterministic cap bucket as names with live readouts. The unresolved event is regulatory: file, then accept, then decide. Corrected to FDA_approval_decision. Note the honest consequence for the CRO: there is no external clock at all until a filing lands. On a submission at the very end of September plus priority review granted, the earliest realistic decision is around mid-2027; on standard review, late 2027. A second, softer leg sits behind it — a supplemental application for toddlers aged 1-3 under the accelerated pathway the FDA agreed in December 2024, guided for end-2026, with the supporting COMFORT safety study having closed recruitment in Q2 2026.

THE SHARE-COUNT CORRECTION (the decisive arithmetic). The board divides by ~62.9M ADS. That is the legal ordinary count only. Reconciliation, all from primary sources: the September 2, 2026 AMF voting-rights release puts total ordinary shares at 314,388,807 as of August 31, 2026 (gross voting rights 314,388,807; net 314,222,095). That ties to the Q2 10-Q cover of 296,061,497 at July 16 plus the ~18.29M ordinary shares placed with RA Capital on July 30 plus ~39k of option/free-share issuance — so the Aug 31 count already includes the ATM and no pre-funded warrants have been exercised. On top of that count sit 100,962,751 pre-funded warrants convertible into 142,647,271 ordinary shares (PFW 2022 13,116,331 -> 13,116,331; PFW1 32,267,060 -> 32,267,060; PFW2 55,579,360 -> 97,263,880). These are not a diluted-count footnote: DBV's own 10-Q calls the remaining cash exercise price immaterial and includes them in BASIC loss per share, which is why the Q2 weighted-average basic count is 433,535,486 ordinary shares against a 296M cover. Economic count = 314,388,807 + 142,647,271 = 457,036,078 ordinary = 91,407,216 ADS at 5 ordinary per ADS. That is 45% above the board basis, and every per-share number in the file inherits it.

NET CASH. $174.9M at June 30, 2026 (cash $23.9M, equivalents $151.0M), no debt — non-current liabilities are $8.5M of leases and employee benefits, current liabilities $54.3M are working capital. Add ~$48.5M net from the $50M gross ATM sale to RA Capital on July 30, less ~2.3 months of burn at ~$12.5M/month (implied by the company's own "$174.9M funds into Q3 2027" runway statement, ~14 months) = ~$28.8M. Net cash at September 8 ~ 174.9 + 48.5 - 28.8 = ~$195M, or $2.13 per ADS on the economic count (the board carried $3.26 per ADS on the wrong divisor).

VALUATION AXES, RE-DERIVED (binary_prob).
Win leg: franchise $2.1B (midpoint of the board's own $1.8-2.4B range, which I did not independently source) + net cash $195M = $2.295B equity; $2.295B / 91,407,216 = $25.11 -> fair_value_target $25. The board's $34 is reproducible only on the wrong divisor ($2.295B/62.9M = $36.5; on a $1.9B franchise, $33.5). The correction is purely the count, not the franchise.
Loss leg: downside_floor $6.75. DBV received a CRL on this exact asset in August 2020 and the stock fell roughly 47% in a session; 13.47 * 0.50 = $6.74. Consistency check: $6.75 * 91.407M = $617M equity = ~$195M cash + ~$422M residual franchise, which is a fair mark for a Phase-3-positive asset held up on CMC and formatting rather than efficacy — a refusal-to-file or CMC CRL here delays the asset, it does not destroy it. Pure-cash floor is $2.13.
win_prob HELD at 0.55, deliberately. Two forces offset and I will not manufacture precision: upward, the primary endpoint was met with the 95% CI lower bound at 24.5% against a 15% bar, breakthrough designation is in hand, and the FDA has requested no additional data; downward, DBV is a two-time regulatory recidivist on this exact patch and the current delay is precisely a CMC/biostatistics packaging problem, which is the historical failure mode.
Resulting EV = 0.55 * 25 + 0.45 * 6.75 = $16.79 vs $13.47 = +24.6% (board +70.6%). R:R = 11.53 / 6.72 = 1.72:1 (board payoff 5.17). Market-implied read on the corrected count: market cap $1.231B, EV ~$1.04B, meaning the tape already pays for roughly half the win-case franchise — a materially less compelling entry than the board's $848M/$645M version.

TAKEOUT LENS — applied, and it does NOT lift the target. DBV is late-stage with pivotal data in hand, so the 2026 regime is nominally in scope, but the only on-point comparable is negative with full provenance: Nestle acquired Aimmune Therapeutics in August 2020 for approximately $2.6B for Palforzia, the peanut-allergy oral immunotherapy; Nestle subsequently took a writedown of roughly $2.4B and divested Palforzia to Stallergenes Greer in 2023. Peanut-allergy immunotherapy has one large real-world commercialization datapoint and it is a value destruction, which is why I decline to lift the win leg on strategic scarcity and why I regard the inherited $1.8-2.4B franchise as generous rather than conservative. Takeout stays unpriced optionality on top of the dated event, never a substitute for it. The regime cuts both ways as flagged: with XBI near a 5-year high, market-implied win probabilities are richer and the old max-fear prints are stale-low, which is a reason my $6.75 floor could prove too harsh — but DBV's own 52-week low of $8.79 was printed before the June filing slip and before the July dilution, so it is not a clean floor either.

WHAT THE CRO SHOULD CARRY FORWARD. The name is not broken and the event is not spent, but it is a soft, twice-guided, company-controlled filing date with no regulator clock behind it, a $150M ATM refreshed on July 17 with $50M already drawn on July 30, and a corrected edge of +25% rather than +71%. Also flag: FMP's quote endpoint returns marketCap $322M for DBVT, roughly 4x too low on either count — do not let that number reach any downstream sizing calculation.

KDP.thesis_summary: KDP is separating its coffee business (Global Coffee Co., which includes US Coffee plus the JDE Peet's assets acquired 1 Apr 2026 for $18.4B) from the North American refreshment-beverage business via a tax-free spin-off targeted for "early 2027" — reaffirmed in the Q2 release of 6 Aug 2026 and the 10-Q of 10 Aug 2026. The trade in KDP common is a sum-of-the-parts re-rating on completion, NOT an index-flow trade: KDP is the RemainCo, retains the ticker, listing and index seat, and index funds are obliged to keep these shares. Whatever forced flow the transaction creates lands on the SpinCo, a security that does not yet exist. The parts are genuinely mismatched — a ~30%-margin US beverage franchise growing sales 10.0% and segment OI 11.9% sits inside the same multiple as a coffee arm whose adjusted OI fell 24.7% y/y on green-coffee costs and tariffs — and the blended entity trades at ~10.6x 2027E EBITDA against parts worth ~11.5-12x. The event itself is real and unfired but carries no binding date, no Form 10 on file as of 25 Aug 2026, no board approval of the distribution, and the company's own stated conditions include "appropriate leverage levels at each company, and supportive market conditions."
KDP.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that completion unlocks an unpaid-for SoP re-rating. Three live facts cut against it. (1) The parts are largely already paid for: sell-side consensus PT is $37.75 (median $38, high $42) versus my $38.50, so the SoP is the consensus view, not a variant one — and the stock is already +12.6% over its 200d MA and 3.9% off its 52-week high, so the discount has been narrowing without the event. (2) The company conditions separation timing on "supportive market conditions" and on reaching appropriate leverage at each entity — by its own language the event is tape-dependent, not idiosyncratic, which is disqualifying for an event-driven sleeve; a risk-off tape both delays the catalyst and de-rates the stock at the same time (correlated, not independent). (3) Execution wobble is real and unresolved: no Form 10 on file at 25 Aug 2026 (a US distribution cannot occur until one is filed and effective, normally 2-4 months ahead), the board has not approved the distribution, and the designated Global Coffee CEO left at end-July 2026 with no successor named — the SpinCo has no CEO roughly five months from its own target window. Secondary: my CoffeeCo leg at 9.5x may itself be generous — US Coffee adjusted OI is running −24.7% y/y and a standalone, levered coffee company carrying green-coffee and tariff cost pass-through could clear at 8x or less, which alone removes ~$2/sh from the target.

This funnel exists to buy defined-risk asymmetry around a scheduled event, and on those terms Bausch + Lomb does not qualify today. A seller with five more years of runway is not a forced seller, which means the forced-seller premise on our board entry is no longer accurate. CELC.dossier_note: This seat existed for one reason: a dated regulatory decision with a spread between the live price and the value the decision would unlock. That decision fired on 14 July 2026, three days early, and it went our way. The position is nonetheless down about 46% from the high. That single fact settles the question this funnel is meant to answer. The discipline here is not to be clever about it. A catalyst that has already resolved is spent, whichever way it resolved. The asymmetry we were paid to underwrite - a hard date, a binding decision, a bounded loss - no longer exists in this name. What remains is a commercial-launch story: whether a first-time commercial company can ship on time, whether oncologists will accept a regimen that produced mouth sores in 58 to 72% of trial patients, and whether a second label arrives before the competition does. Those are perfectly respectable questions. They are not event-driven questions, and they cannot be answered before the first revenue line arrives in early November 2026. The second finding is the one that decides the sizing. The downside floor of $60 carried on the board is not a floor. It is a bear valuation that already assumes the launch broadly works - at $60 the enterprise is worth about $2.79B, which needs peak annual sales above $1.2B. The only hard number underneath is net cash of roughly $140M, about $3 a share. There is no acquirer under contract, no contingent payment right, no recovery value. A defensible adverse case is $5

AQST.thesis_summary: Anaphylm (oral sublingual epinephrine) is on a post-CRL repair path: the Jan-30-2026 CRL deficiencies (human factors, packaging, one supportive PK study) were addressed with clean topline results announced 8/10/26 (pouch-open 17s to 3s, placement errors down >80%, self-admin PK comparable), and management reaffirmed on 8/11 an NDA resubmission on or before 9/30/26. The resubmission is company-controlled and NOT yet filed as of 8/25 (EDGAR through 8/18: only Forms 4 after the 8/10-8/11 disclosures), so no FDA action date exists; a Class 2 classification (new clinical data) implies a six-month review and a decision ~Mar-Apr 2027 on a 9/30 filing. Approval by 2027-06-30 unlocks ~$95M contingent, non-dilutive funding ($75M RTW purchase, $20M Oaktree Tranche B). The edge case has compressed: at 4.80 (8/24 close, $602M mcap) AQST trades ABOVE the approved-and-launched needle-free comp ARS Pharmaceuticals/SPRY (5.35, $531M, ~$117M TTM revenue), so the market-implied win probability is already rich.
AQST.kill_risk: The catalyst is still self-declared: five weeks before the guided 9/30 deadline no resubmission has been filed, and the FDA cannot start a clock on an unfiled application. The new PK and HF studies make Class 2 (six-month review) the likely classification — management itself concedes expedited review cannot be guaranteed — so any slip of the filing into Q4 pushes the decision into Q2-2027, up against the 2027-06-30 RTW/Oaktree approval deadlines: the same slip that costs time forfeits ~$95M of non-dilutive funding on a balance sheet with a $56.6M stockholders' deficit and ~$89M of pre-sold revenue/royalty claims senior to the equity. Meanwhile the price already exceeds the approved comp (SPRY $531M), so even a clean approval may deliver little upside versus the comp-marked win leg (~$5.00).

AMLX.thesis_summary: Amylyx Pharmaceuticals is a single-asset binary into the Phase 3 LUCIDITY topline for avexitide (first-in-class GLP-1 receptor antagonist, FDA Breakthrough Therapy) in post-bariatric hypoglycemia, company-guided to Q3 2026 and reaffirmed in the 7 May 2026 Q1 release. Enrollment closed March 2026 at 78 participants against a 16-week FDA-agreed primary endpoint (composite rate of Level 2 and Level 3 hypoglycemic events), so the last Week-16 visit fell ~mid-July and the print is mechanically due. Verified unfired as of 2026-08-04: latest 8-K is 4 June 2026, latest substantive press release 23 June 2026 (Phase 1 LUMINA ALS at ENCALS), and the only newer item is an 3 Aug 2026 notice that Q2 results come 6 August 2026. The event is fully idiosyncratic - it resolves on trial data, not on the tape. The correction versus the board is on the axes, not the catalyst: the stock has re-rated to $20.17 (52-week range $7.48-$20.94, 200-day $14.83), the downside leg is net cash of roughly $2.13/share at 30 June, not $4, and on a defensible $30 win leg the market-implied win probability is already ~64% - at or above my own ~62% estimate. The asymmetry this funnel hunts existed near $8; what remains is a fairly-priced coin flip with an 88% loss leg.
AMLX.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is "an unfired, mechanically-due pivotal binary with defined downside". Both halves are attackable from the live record. (1) The price has already discounted the win: on my legs the breakeven probability is (20.17-2.50)/(30-2.50) = 64.3%, above my 62% fundamental estimate, so the expected value is roughly flat-to-slightly-negative rather than the +45% the board carries - the edge was in the $8-14 tape, not at a 52-week high. (2) The evidentiary prior is thinner than "pivotal-ready" implies: the supporting work is a Phase 2 PREVENT crossover of N=18 (40-55% event reduction) and an N=16 open-label investigator-initiated Phase 2b; a 78-patient parallel-group read on a variable, event-count endpoint with real placebo response is not the same experiment, and Breakthrough designation is not evidence of effect size. (3) The downside is not defined in any protective sense: the same management team's prior binary (AMX0035 PHOENIX) closed $18.97 on 7 Mar 2024 and $3.36 on 8 Mar 2024, -82% in one session, resting at $1.62 by June 2024 - and that shell held more cash per share than AMLX will hold at the LUCIDITY print, so $2.50 is a mark, not a floor; $1.60-2.00 is inside precedent. (4) Timing residual: "Q3 2026" is a company-guided quarter window, not a PDUFA-style binding date, and slip into Q4 is possible - the 6 August 2026 Q2 call is the next checkpoint that would confirm or break the September end-stop.

AAUC.thesis_summary: Zijin Gold's C$44.00-per-share all-cash takeover of Allied Gold, about US$31.17, hits its contractual deadline on 29 July 2026 with the shares at US$20.85 - roughly 50% below the cash price - because the last outstanding condition is an undated Chinese outbound-investment approval whose stated objection, that the premium is too high, has been strengthened by a 28% fall in gold since signing; about 50% upside against roughly 21% downside to an estimated standalone value near US$16.50.
AAUC.dated_milestone: 29 July 2026 - the contractual outside date, the last day the arrangement can close without a further extension. Critically, this is a walk-away date, not a decision date: it is the day termination rights arise, and it says nothing about when the outstanding approval will be granted. The deadline has already moved once, from 29 May 2026, using an extension right built into the agreement; the company's 29 May release states that any further extension requires the parties' mutual agreement, so that automatic mechanism is now spent. Approvals confirmed to date: shareholder vote 31 March 2026 at 99.54%; Canada's foreign-investment review completed 29 May 2026; West African and East and Southern African regional competition clearances 29 May 2026; Ethiopia around 14 July 2026. Outstanding: approval from China's National Development and Reform Commission, which has no statutory clock and has published no timetable. A trade report dated 21 July 2026 states the regulator is weighing Malian security conditions and questioning the 27% premium, and that Zijin's investor relations declined to give any timing guidance eight days before the deadline. Verified 28 July 2026 against company releases of 29 May and 10 June 2026, the 21 July trade report, and market data as of the 27 July close.
AAUC.kill_risk: [CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTIONS] The asymmetry itself survives primary-source attack, but the file's DECISIVE bear pillar is contractually false. The dossier states in five separate places that the automatic extension right is 'spent' / 'exhausted', so that any third deadline requires Zijin to affirmatively re-commit to a January price - this is the load-bearing reason the 29 July date is framed as a forcing event and the reason the break branch carries 45% weight. CAPR.thesis_summary: Binary FDA decision on deramiocel (allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cell therapy) in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, resolving on a hard PDUFA date of 22 November 2026. The record changed twice since the board's 8 June asof: on 29 July 2026 the Cellular, Tissue and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee voted 9-3 AGAINST substantial evidence of effectiveness for the DMD-CARDIOMYOPATHY indication (8-K filed 30 July; stock lost ~64% around the briefing documents, a ~$15.08/share decline, and printed a 52-week low of $2.96); then on 24 August 2026 Capricor disclosed that the FDA had classified its amendment as a MAJOR AMENDMENT and pushed the action date from 22 August to 22 November 2026. The amendment repositions the ask onto the HOPE-3 PRIMARY endpoint the trial actually hit -- upper limb function, PUL v2.0, 54% slowing of decline, p=0.029, with LVEF 91% slowing, p=0.041 as key secondary, published in The Lancet 29 July -- plus 24-month open-label-extension data. So the panel's negative vote was on a question the company is no longer asking, and the FDA chose to extend rather than act on 22 August. That is the whole trade: a narrower, better-evidenced label sought late in a review cycle whose panel already said no once. Idiosyncratic, unfired, 75 days out.

CAPR.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the upper-limb amendment is a live approval path rather than a deferred refusal, and it does not survive a hard look. (1) The only panel that has voted on deramiocel voted 9-3 against; the committee was never asked to vote on the HOPE-3 primary endpoint or on benefit-risk, so there is NO endorsement of the upper-limb case — the "directionally supportive" characterization of that discussion comes from Capricor's own 30 July press release, not from the agency. (2) A major amendment that changes the proposed indication this late is routinely handled by CBER as a new review problem; extending the clock buys review time, it is not a signal of intent, and the modal outcome of "FDA needed three more months after its panel said no" is a complete response letter with a resubmission invitation, which resolves the trade to the floor even though the program survives. (3) The efficacy rests on ONE adequate and well-controlled trial at p=0.029 on a functional scale whose clinical meaningfulness the agency contested in the briefing documents; substantial evidence from a single trial plus confirmatory evidence is discretionary, and the discretion here sits with reviewers who just published a negative assessment. (4) Balance-sheet asymmetry runs the wrong way in the refusal branch: the 9 July HQ/cleanroom lease (8-K filed 14 July, ~171,000 sq ft, ~$958k/month base rent, 138-month term, ~$136M undiscounted base rent) commences on the EARLIER of the approval contingency or 31 December 2026, so it lands whether or not the drug is approved unless a party terminates inside a five-business-day window after that date. (5) A securities class action covering 17 Dec 2025-26 Jul 2026 with a 28 September lead-plaintiff deadline sits on top, and a CRL in November would arrive with ~$175M of cash against a ~$13M/month all-in burn — survivable, but a financing on a broken chart.

CATALYST CHAIN, VERIFIED FROM PRIMARY SOURCES. 27 Jul 2026 — Capricor comments on FDA briefing materials (company PR); stock falls ~64%, class actions plead a $15.08/share decline. 29 Jul 2026 — Cellular, Tissue and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee votes 3 for / 9 against / 0 abstaining that available evidence supports effectiveness of deramiocel for DMD CARDIOMYOPATHY (8-K filed 30 Jul); The Lancet publishes HOPE-3 the same day. 13 Aug 2026 — Q2 results (8-K, Item 2.02 only; no financing). 14 Aug 2026 — 10-Q. 24 Aug 2026 — 8-K and PR: FDA classifies the amendment (24-month HOPE-3 open-label-extension data plus analyses supporting a refined indication focused on UPPER LIMB FUNCTION) as a MAJOR AMENDMENT, extending the action date three months from 22 Aug to 22 NOV 2026. No company press release since 24 Aug; the entire September tape is plaintiffs'-bar reminders of the 28 Sep lead-plaintiff deadline (class period 17 Dec 2025 - 26 Jul 2026). NO second advisory committee has been announced — that remains the single largest process unknown into November, and its absence cuts both ways: no new negative vote, but also no forum in which the upper-limb case gets a public endorsement.

MILESTONE SLIP, NAMED: 2026-08-22 -> 2026-11-22, cause = FDA major-amendment classification of Capricor's own submission (i.e. a company-initiated slip the agency accepted, not an agency stall). Unfired and idiosyncratic: it resolves on CBER's reading of one trial, not on the tape.

WHY THE PANEL VOTE IS NOT DISPOSITIVE — AND WHY THAT IS NOT A FREE PASS. HOPE-3 MET its primary endpoint (upper limb function, PUL v2.0, 54% slowing of decline, p=0.029) and its key secondary (LVEF, 91% slowing, p=0.041). The BLA as filed sought CARDIOMYOPATHY, which rested on the cardiac secondary plus HOPE-2, and that is the question the panel voted down 9-3. The amendment moves the ask onto the endpoint the trial actually hit. Against that: the committee was never asked to vote on the primary endpoint or on overall benefit-risk, and the "directionally supportive" gloss on its upper-limb discussion is Capricor's own characterization in its 30 July release, not an agency statement. Net, I mark the win leg at 35% versus the 20-25% post-negative-panel base rate the prior record derived for the ORIGINAL question, and versus the ~31% the market itself implies at $9.40 on my own two legs.

VALUATION ARITHMETIC (binary_prob, ~58.1M shares). WIN $24.00: market-implied route — pre-briefing-document price ~$23.5 embedded roughly a two-thirds chance of a BROADER cardiomyopathy label across essentially all DMD patients, so certainty on a NARROWER non-ambulatory upper-limb label is worth about the same, not more; commercial route — ~1,300 treated US patients at ~$500k/yr = ~$650M peak sales, 4x peak-sales EV = ~$2.6B = ~$45/share, discounted three years at 25% = ~$23/share. Both land at $23-25. LOSE $2.75: 30 Jun cash + investments $237.93M, less ~4.7 months at the H1 all-in rate of ~$12.9M/month (operating $60.7M + capex $16.6M = $77.3M in six months) = ~$177M at the decision; less AP/accrued $19.47M and lease obligations $91.05M = $66.5M = $1.14/share structural, against an actual post-panel max-fear print of $2.96 (52-week low). $2.75 splits them and docks the $2.96 print for five more months of burn and for the fact that a November refusal also kills the pivot. At $9.40 that is R:R 2.20:1 and EV $10.19 (+8.4%) — thin, honest, and a long way from the board's $38.50.

TAKEOUT LENS (applied, deliberately NOT credited to the target). The 2026 late-stage biotech M&A regime is real, but this asset is encumbered: Nippon Shinyaku already holds US and Japan commercialization rights to deramiocel, which is the standard reason a would-be acquirer walks. The plausible buyer set is therefore short and led by Nippon Shinyaku itself taking the asset outright; a DMD-adjacent strategic is a distant second. I could not verify a named, dated, valued comparable takeout in this session, so per the provenance rule the win leg is NOT lifted — takeout stays undated optionality sitting on top of the 22 November event, never a substitute for it. ANNX.thesis_summary: Annexon reads out the Month 15 primary endpoint of the Phase 3 ARCHER II trial of vonaprument in geographic atrophy in Q4 2026 — a dated, forward, unfired, idiosyncratic trial readout, reconfirmed in the 12-Aug-2026 Q2 release and on the 19-Aug earnings call. The endpoint is BCVA >=15-letter loss, a functional VISION endpoint, which is what makes the asset differentiated: both approved GA drugs (Apellis SYFOVRE, Astellas Izervay) are anatomical lesion-growth agents with no demonstrated vision benefit, and fewer than 10% of diagnosed GA patients are treated today. Behind the GA event sits a second, largely independent asset — tanruprubart in Guillain-Barre syndrome, BLA submission guided for Q4 2026 with an EU MAA under EMA review since Jan-2026, which would be the first approved disease-modifying therapy in an indication with ~150,000 cases/yr and zero approved options. The structure of the trade changed materially on 12-Aug-2026, when the company added a Month 24 dual primary endpoint (independent timepoint, 2027) plus an open-label extension: a Month 15 miss is no longer terminal, and the 30-Jul-2026 Oxford Finance facility (up to $200M, $50M drawn) plus $209.2M of cash funds the company to reach that second shot. Both the board's win leg and the skeptic's floor were derived before these facts and are corrected below.
ANNX.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that a positive Month 15 BCVA result is genuinely achievable and that the Month 24 dual primary is a real second shot rather than a tell. The live record pushes back hard. Adding a Month 24 primary endpoint in the final quarter before an M15 readout, announced in the same release as an OLE launch and two weeks after drawing $50M of senior secured debt, is the pattern of a sponsor building a landing pad; the market read it that way and marked the stock down ~6%, and analysts on the 19-Aug call pressed management directly on whether it signalled concern about M15 (management said M15 remains the base case). Substantively: neither approved GA drug has ever shown a functional vision benefit, and vonaprument's own vision signal comes from a Phase 2 (ARCHER) that MISSED its primary anatomical endpoint — the prospective functional endpoint is unproven in this mechanism and this class. Second residual: my $2.85 floor is a modelled intrinsic, not an observed clearing price. The 52-week low of $2.10 was printed on a weaker balance sheet but also a cleaner setup, and a post-miss print in the low $2s or below is entirely plausible before the market gives the M24 shot or the GBS asset any credit — small-cap biotech overshoots through intrinsic on a failed pivotal. Treat $2.85 as the funded intrinsic and the low $2s as the tape risk.

The core judgement is straightforward. Scholar Rock has a hard, dated, binding regulatory decision 65 days away, and the reason the last one went wrong has been engineered around rather than merely promised away. WBD.thesis_summary: Paramount Skydance is acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery for $31.00/share ALL CASH ($81B equity, ~$110B EV incl. ticking fee); WBD holders approved, DOJ cleared, and the European Commission formally cleared on 2026-07-22. The sole remaining gate is a 12-state antitrust suit before Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin (N.D. Cal.), which has stopped the deal cold: a TRO was granted 2026-07-20 and extended, and on 2026-07-24 Paramount STIPULATED it will not consummate until the earlier of a merits ruling or 2027-06-01. Paramount then abandoned the preliminary-injunction stage entirely - its counsel concluded plaintiffs would likely prevail at PI - and cancelled the 2026-08-03 hearing in favour of a speedy merits trial. Trial date is NOT set: Paramount wants November 2026, the states asked for a 12-15 day trial starting 2027-04-05. The event is real, forward-dated, unfired and idiosyncratic (it resolves on a courtroom ruling, not the tape), but it is no longer a dated Q3-2026 convergence - it is a ~10-month legal binary with a ticking-fee carry of only ~$0.25/share/quarter starting 2026-09-30.
WBD.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim in the thesis is the cushioned break leg: that a blocked deal pays WBD the $7B reverse-termination fee (+$2.79/sh), holding the floor near $17. Two live refutations. (1) The RTF is payable only on a REGULATORY termination as defined in the merger agreement; a negotiated walk-away, a Paramount financing failure (Larry Ellison personally guaranteed $40.4B, collateral tied to Oracle stock), or a mutual termination on other grounds may not trigger it - the floor then collapses toward the naked standalone $12-17. (2) More probable and priced by neither of my legs: with a ~1-year delay, Paramount's own concession that it would lose the PI, and $9.8B of total Ellison break exposure, the realistic middle path is a RENEGOTIATED LOWER price or a restructured deal (e.g. carving out the assets the states object to), not a clean $31.75 vs $17.00 binary. A cut to, say, $27-28 leaves the buyer at ~breakeven against today's $26.09 while I have carried ten months of dead time. Secondary: my 0.55 win_prob sits BELOW the ~0.62 undiscounted market-implied, and the bull rebuttal is strong - state AGs rarely succeed in blocking a merger their federal counterpart has already cleared, and both DOJ and the EC have cleared this one. A second regulatory front is also still open in the UK, where producers and talent are lobbying the culture minister to intervene.

The event is real, forward-dated, unfired and idiosyncratic — it resolves on FDA's own review, not the tape. The asset would be first-in-disease (no approved therapy for aPAP), carries Fast Track, Breakthrough, Orphan and EU/UK designations, with EPO and Australian formulation patents to March 2041, and the 15 April 2026 three-month extension (from 22 Aug to 22 Nov) was a major-amendment clock reset that cited no safety, efficacy or manufacturing concern. The load-bearing correction is arithmetic, not narrative: the board's per-share axes were divided by 204.9m common shares, but Savara's fully-participating equity base is 254.0m units, because 48,600,212 pre-funded warrants struck at $0.001 with NO expiration are outstanding and the issuer itself includes them in basic EPS (Q2 weighted-average denominator 253,569,891, printing $(0.16) on a $40.2m loss — $(0.20) on the board's base). Re-dividing the board's own franchise-PV build by the correct base moves the win leg from $8.00 to $6.45 and the loss leg from $1.50 to $1.21. At $5.37 that is +20.1% up / -77.5% down, a 0.26:1 payoff and a 79.4% break-even probability against the ~80% first-cycle approval odds I can honestly defend — so the catalyst layer is clean and the edge is approximately zero, not the +30.8% the board carries.
SVRA.kill_risk: The 254.0m denominator itself survives every refutation I could mount (the pre-funded warrants have no expiry, a $0.001 strike, and GAAP basic-EPS inclusion by the issuer; beneficial-ownership blockers gate WHEN a holder exercises, never economic participation), so the residual risk is not the share count — it is that my $1.21 loss leg is still too generous and the ~80% win probability too high for an INHALED BIOLOGIC. Device/CMC is the single most common CRL cause for inhalation products, and this BLA already absorbed a major-amendment extension driven by FDA information requests; "no concern cited" in an extension letter is not a clean-review signal, only the absence of a stated one. On a CRL the loss leg carries a financing event on top of the re-rating: RTW's $75.0m royalty purchase is payable only "upon approval of MOLBREEVI by the FDA on or before March 31, 2027" (10-Q Note 9), and a Class 2 resubmission starts a fresh six-month clock only once filed, so a 22 Nov CRL forfeits that $75m permanently rather than deferring it — while the Hercules Cash Requirement covenant goes live 1 April 2027 against roughly $88m of net cash. The $1.21 embeds ~$220m of residual pipeline option value above cash; a real CRL tape would likely print below it, and the 52-week low of $3.34 is not a max-fear comp because it predates any rejection. Separately, the win leg is a ceiling rather than a midpoint: the board's franchise PV discounts US gross margins with no deduction for the 7.0%-to-9.5% tiered US royalty (capped at a $187.5m Maximum Payment) that Savara has already TRUE-SOLD to RTW.

SVRA.dossier_note:
CATALYST — CONFIRMED CLEAN. PDUFA target action date 22 November 2026 for MOLBREEVI (molgramostim inhalation solution) in autoimmune PAP, stated verbatim in the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 Jun 2026 (accepted 2026-08-11, EDGAR CIK 0001160308, svra-20260630.htm) and in the 11 Aug Q2 release. History: original PDUFA was 22 Aug 2026; on 15 Apr 2026 FDA ruled the company's responses to information requests a MAJOR AMENDMENT and extended three months to 22 Nov, citing no safety, efficacy or manufacturing concern. That slip is already reflected in the board's milestone, so the status is PENDING_HARD, not SLIPPED. No 8-K has been filed since 8 Jun 2026 and no news exists between 31 Aug and 8 Sep 2026 — no approval, no CRL, no further extension. Newest flow is non-eventful: ERS Barcelona ENCORE presentations of IMPALA-2 (5-9 Sep 2026, announced 24 Aug) — encore data, not new data, no informational content for the decision. Idiosyncratic: resolves on FDA's review of one BLA.

THE DENOMINATOR — THIS IS THE WHOLE CORRECTION. Primary source, 10-Q Note 8 "Common Stock Reserved for Issuance", 30 Jun 2026: Pre-funded PIPE Warrants 3,615,516 + 2021 Pre-funded 32,175,172 + 2023 Pre-funded 5,666,667 + 2025 Pre-funded 7,142,857 = 48,600,212, and the warrant table lists all 48,600,212 at a $0.001 exercise price with expiration date "None". Balance sheet: 205,399,365 common shares issued and outstanding. Fully-participating base = 205,399,365 + 48,600,212 = 253,999,577 (254.0m). The issuer agrees: Note 12 computes basic EPS on "the weighted-average number of common stock AND pre-funded warrants outstanding", and the Q2 table prints weighted-average 253,569,891 shares, $(40,228)k net loss, $(0.16) per share. On the board's 204.9m that same loss prints $(0.20). The company's own filing refutes the board's base.

RE-DERIVED AXES (board's aggregate valuation, correct base). Win leg: $8.00 x 204.9m = $1.639bn equity value / 254.0m = $6.45. Loss leg: $1.50 x 204.9m = $307m / 254.0m = $1.21. Net cash today: $41.8m cash + $131.2m short-term investments − $30.1m long-term (Hercules) debt = $142.9m = $0.56/unit (the board's "$0.70 of net cash" is the same $142.9m over the wrong base). At the 22 Nov decision date, at the 1H run-rate of $62.8m operating cash use per six months stepped up for the commercial build (~$11.5m/mo x 4.75mo ≈ $55m), net cash ≈ $88m ≈ $0.35/unit. R:R at $5.37: +20.1% up, −77.5% down, payoff 0.26:1. Break-even probability = (5.37 − 1.21) / (6.45 − 1.21) = 4.16 / 5.24 = 79.4%. I underwrite 80%, so EV = 0.80 x 6.45 + 0.20 x 1.21 = $5.40, or +0.6% — a coin-flip-fair binary, versus the board's +30.8%. Note the board's OWN ev_pct/payoff/win_prob triple is internally consistent only on 204.9m; nothing here is a judgement change, it is the same model over the share count the issuer reports.

WHY $6.45 IS A CEILING, NOT A MIDPOINT. 10-Q Note 9: on 29 Oct 2025 Savara TRUE-SOLD to RTW Investments US royalties of 7.0% of net sales tiered down to 1.0%, with the 7.0% tier ratcheting to 9.5% if a prior-year sales level is missed, running until RTW receives a $187.5m Maximum Payment. A franchise PV built on unencumbered orphan-biologic gross margin does not deduct that stream; the offsetting $75.0m receipt is already inside the cash bridge below. Treat $6.45 as the generous end.

THE LOSS LEG CARRIES A FINANCING EVENT. RTW's $75.0m is payable only "upon approval of MOLBREEVI by the FDA on or before March 31, 2027" (Note 9). A CRL on 22 Nov 2026 followed by a Class 2 resubmission starts a six-month review clock only once the response is FILED — even a January 2027 filing lands past 31 Mar 2027. So rejection does not defer the facility, it forfeits half the $150m non-dilutive package permanently, while the Hercules First Amendment makes the Cash Requirement covenant live 1 April 2027 against roughly $88m of net cash. $1.21 implies ~$220m of residual pipeline option above cash (EU MAA and UK MHRA still under review, IPR&D $11.3m, patents to 2041); that is defensible but soft — a real CRL tape plausibly prints below it. The 52-week low of $3.34 is NOT a max-fear comp: it predates any rejection scenario.

TAKEOUT LENS (bio, per the 2026 M&A regime note) — NO LIFT TAKEN, and no milestone created. SVRA has pivotal data in hand and is ~75 days from a decision on a first-in-disease orphan biologic with 2041 formulation IP, which is squarely the profile the 2026 tape rewards, and plausible acquirers are the rare-respiratory/rare-disease consolidators (GSK, which already bought respiratory-adjacent late-stage risk this year; AstraZeneca; a rare-disease buyer such as Sanofi or CSL). But the comps I can actually provenance are an order of magnitude larger and therefore do not scale onto a ~$1.4bn name: GSK / Nuvalent, announced 9 Jun 2026, ~$10.6bn equity value for a ROS1 asset UNDER FDA review; Vertex / Crinetics, announced 6 Jul 2026, $85/share cash, ~$10.0bn, a 102% premium. Both confirm buyers will pay for pre-approval rare/targeted assets, neither defends moving $6.45 up. Takeout stays undated optionality ON TOP of the 22 Nov event, never a substitute for it. The regime caveat cuts against us here as much as for us: with XBI at a five-year high, the market-implied probability embedded in $5.37 is RICHER than a max-fear tape would set — the implied 79.4% is close to the clinical base rate, which is precisely why the corrected edge is ~0 rather than negative-and-obvious.

PROCESS FLAG for the Director: an 18 Aug 2026 skeptic pass raised this identical pre-funded-warrant denominator error and the record was rewritten still dividing by 204.9m. This dossier is the second correction of the same defect; the FMP market-cap field ($1.100bn on common only) is the likely upstream source, so any other single-asset name in the sleeve with a large pre-funded warrant block should be assumed to carry the same error until checked.

Stock at $12.255 vs $16.00 is a 30.6% gross spread, i.e. the market prices roughly a coin-flip on completion, not a normal late-stage arb. Timeline has slipped twice (contractual outside date 2026-05-11 already extended to 2026-08-10, further extension to 2026-11-10 available while regulatory approval is pending); Western Union's 2026-07-30 Q2 guidance now assumes a 2026-09-01 close. RARE.thesis_summary: Ultragenyx (RARE, $15.30 at the 9/4 close, last print before Labor Day) carries an unslipped, agency-assigned PDUFA goal date of 19 Sep 2026 on the resubmitted UX111 (rebisufligene etisparvovec) BLA for Sanfilippo type A, priority review, accelerated-approval pathway, no AdCom. The July 2025 CRL was CMC/inspection-only (10-Q language: observations at Ultragenyx's own gene-therapy facility and at a third-party manufacturer; no clinical deficiency). On 19 Aug 2026 the FDA approved GENGLYCOS (DTX401) four days early off the same Ultragenyx facility and issued a priority review voucher, a live third-party test of the facility objection. The event is idiosyncratic: it resolves on the CMC record, not on the tape, and is unaffected by the 2 Sep Aspire (apazunersen/Angelman) failure that cut the stock 44% and reset the value stack. Approval adds roughly $3.2/sh of hard value (UX111 product ~$150m + a second saleable PRV ~$175m on 101.9m economic shares) and removes the manufacturing overhang from the whole gene-therapy platform; win-leg SoP value ~$19.50, lose-leg ~$12.35, ~72% approval odds, EV ~$17.50 (+14%), R:R ~1.4:1.
RARE.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the 19 Aug GENGLYCOS approval cleared the objection behind the UX111 CRL. It only partly does: the 10-Q states the July 2025 CRL cited observations at BOTH Ultragenyx's own gene-therapy facility AND a third-party manufacturer, and UX111 (AAV9, ex-Abeona) does not necessarily share DTX401's (AAV8) third-party site or process. A residual CMC finding at the third-party site, or a CBER request for a major amendment that extends the goal date by three months (SLIPPED, not lost), remains credible. Secondary: the approval sought is accelerated and biomarker-based (CSF heparan sulfate) with confirmatory obligations, and CBER has walked back biomarker pathways for other AAV programs in 2025-26. Also, the board's floor is a valuation floor with no contractual backstop; the prior $18 floor of identical construction broke 25% in one session on 3 Sep.

CMCSA.thesis_summary: Comcast announced 2026-06-29 (8-K Ex-99.1) its intention to separate into two public companies via a tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal + Sky, "expected to be completed in approximately one year" (i.e. ~mid-2027). RemainCo = domestic broadband/wireless/business services on the 65m-home converged network (Michael Angelakis CEO); SpinCo = Universal parks/studios, NBC/Telemundo, Peacock, Bravo and Sky (Mike Cavanagh CEO). The trade is a sum-of-the-parts re-rate: the consolidated entity trades at ~4.85x EV/EBITDA (EV $169.9B on $87.2B cap + $82.7B Q2-2026 net debt, over ~$35B FY26E adjusted EBITDA), while the live comps are CHTR at 5.70x and DIS at 10.81x EV/EBITDA TTM. Marking the parts at 5.5x / 7.5x on 2027E gets ~$34/sh vs $24.56 spot. Carry is paid by the $0.33/qtr dividend declared 2026-07-23 (5.4% yield, covered ~3.5x by H1-26 FCF of $8.5B).
CMCSA.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is "the parts re-rate." Three live facts cut against it. (1) Comcast just ran this experiment: the Versant spin closed 2026-01-02 and the stub went from a $32.86 52-wk high to a $21.28 low - a spin at this issuer has already failed once in seven months to re-rate the remainder. (2) The EBITDA base is eroding faster than the multiple is likely to expand: Q2-26 residential C&P adjusted EBITDA fell 8.0% y/y, domestic broadband revenue -5.5%, 167k broadband subs lost in the quarter, and total adjusted EBITDA fell 5.3% y/y even pro forma for Versant/Sky-Germany. A 23-month hold against a -5%/yr base eats most of a one-turn re-rate. (3) The Disney-multiple analogue is structurally blocked: the 8-K states NBCUniversal will carry "the same dual-class share structure as Comcast" (Roberts control retained) and Comcast keeps up to 19.9% of SpinCo to monetize over time - a governance discount plus a stated overhang, against a single-class DIS comp. Deal risk is also non-trivial and self-declared: final board approval, tax opinions, regulatory approvals and financing are all still outstanding, with "no assurance that the proposed transaction will be completed." Finally, the driver is only semi-idiosyncratic - completion resolves on company facts, but the realized value depends on where the tape chooses to multiple cable and legacy media in mid-2027.

Re-pointed the dossier to the new event; the board's own instrument note ('mid-2027 resolution') already matched it, so the lane was internally inconsistent.

CATALYST. Real, forward-dated, unfired. Tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal + Sky, announced 2026-06-29, headline language: "Expected to be Completed in Approximately One Year." Transaction Details paragraph: "subject to the satisfaction of customary conditions, including final approval by Comcast's Board of Directors, receipt of tax opinions, regulatory approvals and completion of financing arrangements... There can be no assurance that the proposed transaction will be completed." Goldman Sachs and PJT advising; Davis Polk counsel. Two structural terms the board dossier missed: NBCUniversal will have the SAME DUAL-CLASS share structure as Comcast, and Comcast will retain up to a 19.9% stake in NBCUniversal for up to one year post-spin, to be monetized over time. Both are direct headwinds to the "Disney multiple" leg of the thesis and are why I marked SpinCo at 7.5x rather than at Disney's 10.8x.

DO NOT CONFUSE WITH VERSANT. The Versant cable-networks spin COMPLETED 2026-01-02 (confirmed in the Q2-26 release pro-forma language). Sky's Germany operations were SOLD 2026-05-31. Both are fired/closed and carry no remaining edge. Any board record pointing at those is spent.

LIVE INPUTS (Q2-2026, $M). Total adjusted EBITDA 8,902 (-13.4% y/y; -5.3% pro forma). Connectivity & Platforms 7,964 (Residential 6,448, -8.0% y/y; Business Services 1,516, +5.0%). Content & Experiences 1,329 (Media 708, Studios 202, Theme Parks 609, HQ/Other -214, elims +25). Corporate & Other -374. H1-26 adjusted EBITDA 16,831; H1-26 FCF 8,505. Balance sheet 2026-06-30: total debt 90,381, cash 7,661, NET DEBT 82,720. Shares outstanding 3,548,636,613 (10-Q). LIVE COMPS (TTM, 2026-08-03): CHTR EV/EBITDA 5.70x (EV 114.5B). DIS EV/EBITDA 10.81x (EV 212.1B).

SOP ARITHMETIC (2027E, the year the spin lands). Step 1, FY26E run-rate: H1 16,831 x2 = 33.7B; I use 34.5B blended with the Q2 segment annualization. Split: C&P ~31.5B, C&E ~5.0B, corporate ~-1.5B. Step 2, move Sky to SpinCo - Sky's connectivity/video EBITDA currently sits inside Residential C&P (international connectivity revenue 1,246 in Q2; 17.5m international customer relationships). Comcast no longer discloses Sky standalone, so I carry Sky at ~2.8B, down from the ~3.0B last disclosed for FY24 to reflect the Germany disposal. THIS IS THE SOFTEST NUMBER IN THE STACK - every +/-0.5B on Sky moves the target roughly +/-$0.6/sh, and it moves it in opposite directions for the two legs (it shifts EBITDA from a 5.5x bucket to a 7.5x bucket). Step 3, RemainCo 2026E = 31.5 - 2.8 Sky - 1.0 allocated corporate = 27.7B; grown at -5% to 2027E = 26.3B; at 5.5x (a modest premium to CHTR's live 5.70x is NOT assumed - I am marking slightly below the comp) = EV 144.7B. Step 4, SpinCo 2026E = 5.0 C&E + 2.8 Sky - 0.5 standalone dis-synergy = 7.3B; +3% to 2027E = 7.5B; at 7.5x = EV 56.3B. Step 5, total EV 201.0B, less mid-2027E net debt ~80B (roughly flat: ~14B/yr FCF against ~4.7B dividends and ~4B buybacks, plus separation financing), = equity 121.0B over ~3.50B shares = $34.57. I round DOWN to $34.00.

SENSITIVITY BAND. Bear marks (RemainCo 5.0x / SpinCo 6.5x) = $29.1. Base (5.5x / 7.5x) = $34.6. Bull (5.7x CHTR-matched / 10.0x Disney-matched, the CNBC framing) = $41+. The band brackets the sell-side: consensus PT $30.13, Deutsche Bank $32 (upgraded to buy, target cut), Evercore ISI $36 (5.5x EV/EBITDA and 8.8x P/FCF on 2027). I sit at the conservative-middle deliberately, because the bull leg requires a multiple NBCUniversal's dual-class structure and 19.9% overhang argue against.

DOWNSIDE FLOOR $21.00. Two independent supports. (a) The live 52-wk low is $21.28 and it is RECENT - the stock traded $22.04 in late July after the Q2 print, i.e. the low was set AFTER the spin was announced, so it is a post-catalyst max-fear mark rather than a stale pre-announcement print. (b) A ~6.3% yield on the $1.32 declared annual dividend implies $21.00; H1-26 FCF of $8.5B covers H1 dividends of ~$2.4B about 3.5x, so a cut is not the base case and the yield floor should hold absent one. A break of $21 requires the market to price either a dividend cut or an abandoned spin. Structural worst case if the spin is shelved and the whole is re-marked at 4.5x on 2027E consolidated EBITDA of ~33B: EV 148.5B - 82.7B net debt = $18.5/sh, which is the true tail, not the working floor.

R:R at spot = 2.65:1 ($9.44 up to $34.00 / $3.56 down to $21.00).

GLUE.thesis_summary: Monte Rosa's resolving event is the full GFORCE-1 Phase 1 readout for MRT-8102, a wholly-owned oral NEK7-directed molecular glue degrader (NLRP3/IL-1-beta pathway), in subjects at elevated cardiovascular risk. Verified live and unfired as of 8 September 2026: the 6 August 2026 second-quarter release confirmed enrollment and dosing complete across all dose levels including the four-week treatment period and four-week safety follow-up, and reaffirmed the readout as anticipated in the second half of 2026. Identical guidance appeared on 7 May 2026, so the timeline has not slipped. It is a guidance WINDOW, not a date: no venue, no presentation slot, no regulatory deadline, nothing contractually owed on any day; the company controls both timing and framing and the window runs to 31 December 2026. The January 2026 interim was a partial slice (roughly 85 percent median CRP reduction at four weeks, 94 percent of subjects below 2 mg/L); the complete dataset, the full dose range and the calprotectin biomarker are still unreleased, so the edge is unspent. The event is idiosyncratic — it resolves on the company's own trial data. What has changed since the board struck this dossier on 8 June 2026 is the underwriting basis, not the event: on 31 July 2026 Novo Nordisk's Phase 3 ZEUS trial of ziltivekimab (IL-6 antibody, over 6,300 ASCVD/CKD patients with hsCRP >= 2 mg/L) missed its primary endpoint with a hazard ratio of 0.99 (95% CI 0.88-1.11) despite confirmed target engagement and the expected free-IL-6 and hsCRP reductions, with more serious infections than placebo. GFORCE-1 reports the same class of biomarker that ZEUS just showed does not predict outcomes. The catalyst remains live, but its power to force a re-rating in the atherosclerotic cardiovascular indication is substantially impaired, and every valuation axis on this record has to be re-cut ex-ASCVD.
GLUE.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that a technically clean GFORCE-1 readout re-rates GLUE toward the ex-ASCVD parts. Four live facts attack it. (1) ZEUS proved that suppressing precisely the biomarker GFORCE-1 reports (free IL-6 / hsCRP) does not translate into outcomes, so a clean CRP result invites a shrug or an outright sell-the-news. (2) The market has already seen the punchline: the January 2026 interim showed roughly 85 percent median CRP reduction and 94 percent of subjects below 2 mg/L, and the stock is nonetheless down 42 percent since 1 July. The full dataset is confirmatory, not revelatory. (3) The company is still guiding a Phase 2 in elevated atherosclerotic risk and cardiometabolic syndrome in H2 2026 — post-ZEUS that reads as capital allocation into a refuted hypothesis and can be taken negatively on the same day the data print. (4) There is no forcing function: $626.0M funds operations into 2029 and the lead wholly-owned asset is Phase 1, so management can release this as a poster or a conference slide at a time of its choosing with no obligation to frame it as an event at all. A soft, undated, self-published biomarker readout in a mechanism the tape has just discounted is the weakest form of catalyst on this board.
