GLUE.dossier_note:
RE-UNDERWRITE AS OF 2026-09-08. Live price 13.84 (4 Sep close), market cap 1.169B, 84,479,418 shares outstanding per the Q2 10-Q cover, 52wk 4.79-25.77, 50d avg 19.01, 200d avg 18.52. Catalyst confirmed live, unfired, undated.

CASH ARITHMETIC (the board and the prior skeptic both got pieces of this wrong). Company-stated 626.0M cash, equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities at 30 Jun 2026 = 7.41/sh gross on 84.48M shares. Total debt 37.99M (largely the facility obligation), so net cash at 30 Jun = 588.0M = 6.96/sh. Burn run-rate, measured not asserted: cash plus short-term investments went 666.2M (31 Mar) -> 621.1M (30 Jun), a 45.1M quarterly decline; net loss was 44.5M in Q1 and 43.4M in Q2 (retained earnings -477.2 -> -521.7 -> -565.1). So ~180M/yr, NOT the 210M/yr the board's sop_bear asserted and then mis-multiplied. Two quarters to a 31 Dec readout at ~48M (R&D is ramping with three Phase 2 starts) = ~96M. Pro-forma year-end: ~530M gross = 6.28/sh, ~492M net of debt = 5.83/sh. I use 5.90/sh in the win stack and 5.80/sh as the floor base — and I use the SAME dated balance in both legs, which the board's stack did not (it banked the un-burned 7.34/sh in the bull case while burning it down in the bear case, widening its own spread by ~1.23/sh for free).

WIN LEG 19.50 (sum of parts, ex-ASCVD-outcome-value). 5.90 pro-forma net cash + 3.50 Novartis MRT-6160/DDY391 (150M upfront received Oct 2024, up to 2.1B milestones, 30% US profit share, and per the 6 Aug 2026 release Novartis has now ACTIVATED the Phase 2a/b in Sjogren's disease at its own cost — the single most de-risked piece on the page) + 1.75 Roche collaboration plus MRT-2359 plus CCNE1 (MRT-2359 is no longer preclinical optionality: first patient was dosed in MODeFIRe-1, a Phase 2 with apalutamide in AR-mutant mCRPC, on 24 Aug 2026) + 8.00 for MRT-8102 as a first-in-class wholly-owned oral NEK7 degrader carrying two funded Phase 2 starts (gout flares Q4 2026/Q1 2027, hidradenitis suppurativa H1 2027). The 8.00 is the whole argument and it is deliberately below the ~14/sh the street carried pre-ZEUS: a Phase 1 biomarker asset with no Phase 2 started in either commercial indication cannot hold a pre-ZEUS ASCVD mark. Sum = 19.15, called 19.50. NOTE ON THE STREET CROSS-CHECK: current consensus is 26.67 (median 27, high 28, low 25) and — contrary to the prior skeptic's framing — the Wedbush 27 (31 Jul) and Guggenheim 28 (6 Aug) marks are POST-ZEUS, so the street did re-underwrite after the miss. I still decline to use them as corroboration, for the reason the skeptic identified: a parts stack that writes ASCVD to zero cannot be validated by targets that carry ASCVD. Landing on the street number would prove the stack is quietly carrying the thing it claims to exclude.

FLOOR 8.00. Bad-readout state: mediocre dose-response, a safety or infection signal, or simply 'clean CRP, so what' after ZEUS. Base is 5.80/sh pro-forma year-end net cash. Multiple: this exact company printed 4.80-4.89 (52wk low 4.79) in September 2025 against roughly 4.08/sh net cash, about 1.18x, with the Novartis license already signed since October 2024 and Roche live — so at real despair the market paid roughly 0.7/sh for the entire partner-and-platform stack. That is the hard floor and it maps to ~6.85 today. I mark 8.00 (~1.4x) rather than 6.85 because the state of the world genuinely improved: Novartis is now funding a Phase 2, MRT-2359 is dosing in a Phase 2, and the January interim data exist. A board floor of 11 (1.9x net cash) is above where this company traded with a better asset base and is not defensible.

ARITHMETIC CHECK. EV = 0.45 x 19.50 + 0.55 x 8.00 = 8.775 + 4.400 = 13.175 versus 13.84 = -4.8%. Payoff +40.9% / -42.2% = 0.97:1. The name is priced roughly fair to slightly rich into its own catalyst. I own the facts and the axes only; the CRO owns whether that is tradeable.

TAKEOUT LENS (bio, per the 2026-07-21 addendum) — DOES NOT APPLY AND I HAVE NOT LIFTED THE WIN LEG. The 2026 M&A regime is running at a record pace for LATE-STAGE, commercially-ready assets. GLUE's lead wholly-owned asset is Phase 1 with Phase 2 not yet started in either target indication; there is no pivotal data in hand and nothing near approval. Big pharma's revealed preference here has already been to OPTION the platform (Novartis global license, Roche collaboration) rather than buy the company, which cuts against a takeout premium rather than for it. I found no named comparable takeout with date and value that would underwrite a lift, so per the rule none is applied — takeout is undated optionality sitting on top of the dated event, never a substitute for it, and it must not extend or replace the H2 2026 milestone.

XBI CAVEAT, BOTH DIRECTIONS. With biotech at multi-year highs, market-implied win probabilities are generally richer and old max-fear prints are generally stale-low — which is exactly why I set the floor at 8.00 rather than at the literal 1.18x despair multiple of 6.85. But the caveat gives this name no beta relief on the upside: GLUE fell 42% from 24.02 on 1 July to 13.84 in a strong tape, on its own facts (ZEUS, 31 July). That is idiosyncratic damage, not sector drawdown, and it means the market has already re-rated the CRP mechanism without waiting for GFORCE-1.

IMTX.thesis_summary: Immatics is a binary on anzu-cel (IMA203), a one-time autologous PRAME TCR-T cell therapy, in the randomised Phase 3 SUPRAME trial in previously-treated advanced melanoma (post-PD1), primary endpoint PFS. Phase 1b at RP2D reads 56% cORR / 14.6mo mDOR / 6.1mo mPFS / 16.2mo mOS / 46% 2-yr OS against a physician's-choice control arm that historically delivers ~2-3mo mPFS, so the effect size on offer is large. The resolving event has SLIPPED: 12-May-2026 guidance said pre-specified interim AND final PFS analyses would be triggered in 2026; the 18-Aug-2026 Q2 release replaced both with a single streamlined final analysis at a lower prespecified event count (PFS events accruing slower than modelled), pushing topline to H1-2027 with a BLA in 2027 and no launch before 2028. The only firmly dated event left in the window is ESMO abstract 1955RO on 24-Oct-2026 (first Phase 1b data for the IMA402 PRAME bispecific at RP2D) — real and idiosyncratic, but it does not resolve the binary. On live anchors the trade is a full-price option, not a spread: the win leg re-derives to $14.00 (not the board's $20) and the failure leg to $2.25, giving +61% / -74% from $8.69, an INVERTED 0.82:1 payoff, with market-implied win probability of ~55% already above my blended 45%.
IMTX.dated_milestone: 2026-10-24 — ESMO Congress 2026, Madrid, rapid oral 1955RO, 08:30-10:00 CEST (Schadendorf): first Phase 1b results for IMA402 PRAME TCR bispecific at the RP2D range. This is the ONLY firmly dated, verifiable event and it is NOT the thesis-resolving one. Load-bearing event = SUPRAME Phase 3 PFS topline, guided H1-2027 (undated within a six-month window), BLA 2027; nearest verifiable checkpoint on that path is completion of ~450 randomisations targeted by year-end 2026.
IMTX.kill_risk: My win leg is not an independent valuation — it is a ratio to Iovance, and Iovance's own tape is the weakest link. The $1.75bn filing-stage EV for anzu-cel is set at ~52% of IOVA's live EV of $3.347bn (mkt cap $3.599bn less $251.7m net cash: $297.7m cash+STI, $46.0m leases, 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet). But IOVA closed $8.06 against a 52-week low of $1.76 and a 200-day average of $3.66 — the comp EV is more than double its own 200-day, struck with XBI at 164.17 versus a 52-week low of 88.71, i.e. near a multi-year high. If IOVA mean-reverts toward its 200-day, the anchor EV falls to roughly $1.4bn and my $1.75bn mark for a pre-approval, pre-revenue asset would sit ABOVE the approved incumbent — indefensible — and the win leg compresses to roughly $9-10, which is the current price. So the entire "+61% upside" claim is levered to a comparable trading at a 52-week high in the hottest biotech tape in five years, and the binary would still have three-to-four quarters to run after any comp de-rating. Second, live and specific: the 18-Aug-2026 disclosure that aggregate PFS events are accruing more slowly than modelled forced a re-cut of the analysis to a lower event count. Fewer events means a wider confidence interval on the hazard ratio, and the change was driven by observed data rather than by plan — the company asserts 90% power retained, which is unverifiable from outside. A design amendment made under the data is a genuine statistical-risk flag, not a neutral logistics update. Third, ITT dilution: anzu-cel is autologous, so patients randomised to it who never reach infusion (apheresis, manufacture, lymphodepletion attrition) count against the treatment arm — precisely where single-arm Phase 1b response rates historically fail to translate in this modality.

IMTX.dossier_note:
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-25. Sources: FMP quote/press-release feeds, Immatics Q2-2026 balance sheet and cash-flow statement (filed 18-Aug-2026, CIK 0001809196, EUR reporting currency), Immatics 17-Jul-2026 ESMO announcement, IOVA Q2-2026 balance sheet (filed 06-Aug-2026), live EURUSD 1.16645.

1) CATALYST — REAL, IDIOSYNCRATIC, UNFIRED, BUT SLIPPED. The event layer survives; the timing did not. 12-May-2026: "pre-specified interim and final data analyses are expected to be triggered in 2026." 18-Aug-2026: both replaced by a single streamlined final PFS analysis at a lower prespecified event count, because aggregate PFS events are accruing more slowly than modelled; trial expanded to ~450 patients; topline H1-2027; BLA 2027. FROM 2026 interim + 2026 final -> TO a single H1-2027 final. Registry NCT06743126 carries an estimated primary completion of January 2028, i.e. the registry is looser than the guidance. Nothing here is tape-driven — this resolves on its own trial data. catalyst_live stays true.

2) MILESTONE. The only firmly dated, independently verifiable event is ESMO 24-Oct-2026, 08:30-10:00 CEST, abstract 1955RO, rapid oral, presenter Dirk Schadendorf, "Initial Results with IMA402, a PRAME-Targeted TCR-based Bispecific T-cell Engager in Advanced Solid Tumors" (confirmed against the 17-Jul-2026 company release; ESMO Congress 23-27 Oct 2026, Madrid). DIRECTOR/CRO WARNING: the binary DOES NOT RESOLVE ON 24 OCTOBER. That date prices only the bispecific leg (~$0.25bn of a $2.21bn win-case equity). staging stays TRUE because the load-bearing SUPRAME topline is undated inside a six-month window.

3) VALUATION AXES — binary_prob, both legs corrected, arithmetic shown.
WIN LEG $14.00. Comp verified live rather than asserted: Iovance market cap $3.599bn at $8.06, less net cash of $251.7m ($297.7m cash+short-term investments minus $46.0m lease obligations, 30-Jun-2026) = EV $3.347bn, against FY-2026 guided Amtagvi revenue of $350-370m in the IDENTICAL indication (previously-treated advanced melanoma post-checkpoint) across 95+ authorised treatment centres. Anzu-cel on a clean randomised PFS win is pre-approval, pre-revenue, launch not before 2028, and would take share FROM Amtagvi rather than enter a virgin market — but it earns a real premium to the prior bear mark because a randomised Phase 3 supporting FULL approval is a stronger regulatory position than lifileucel's single-arm accelerated approval, and 56% cORR versus roughly 31% deserves credit. Mark it at $1.75bn, ~52% of the verified incumbent EV. Plus bispecific franchise / IMA203CD8 / Moderna collaboration / discovery engine $0.25bn. Plus residual cash at readout $0.21bn (see below). Equity $2.21bn / ~158m shares = $13.99, carried $14.00. Share bridge: 136.6m today (par value EUR1,366,435 at EUR0.01), ATM drip to ~144m by readout (they took EUR22.1m in Q1-2026 and EUR99.4m in Q4-2025, so the programme is live), then a commercial raise on the win path treated as value-neutral (cash in, consumed by build-out and pre-revenue burn) to ~158m. The raise is now structurally REQUIRED on the win path: runway does not reach first revenue in any outcome.
FAILURE LEG $2.25. EUR393.2m cash+STI at 30-Jun-2026, less four quarters at ~EUR53m (TTM operating outflow EUR206.2m: -61.2 Q2-26, -42.7 Q1-26, -57.6 Q4-25, -44.7 Q3-25, plus ~EUR3.7m capex) = ~EUR183m at a mid-2027 readout = ~$213m, or ~$1.55-1.80 per share on a drifted count. Residual platform on a failure is impaired but not zero at $0.45-0.70. Floor $2.10-2.50, carried $2.25.
WHY $2.25 AND NOT LOWER: the hot-tape caveat cuts in the bull's favour here. XBI is at 164.17 against a 52-week low of 88.71 and within 3% of its high — old max-fear "0.8-1.2x residual net cash" clearing prints for busted biotechs are stale-low in this regime. A second, genuine de-correlation the prior pass missed: IMA402 prints at ESMO in OCTOBER 2026, roughly eight months BEFORE SUPRAME topline. If the bispecific shows real activity in October, the PRAME-target hypothesis is partially validated independently, and the residual leg is no longer purely hostage to the cell-therapy failure. The correlation argument (same antigen, lower-potency modality, therefore impaired on the same day) is directionally right but is largely SETTLED BEFORE the binary resolves, not on it.
CONSEQUENCE. From $8.69: +61.1% to $14.00, -74.1% to $2.25, payoff 0.82:1 — INVERTED. Market-implied win probability = (8.69-2.25)/(14.00-2.25) = 54.8%, at or above my blended 45%. Expected value 0.45 x 14.00 + 0.55 x 2.25 = $7.54, roughly -13% against the traded price BEFORE discounting three to four quarters at a biotech cost of capital. Under the finer frame (35% clean win $14.00, 20% marginal win ~$8.50, 45% failure $2.25) EV is $7.61 — same conclusion. The spread is already gone.

4) TAKEOUT LENS — ASSESSED, NO LIFT TAKEN, AND DELIBERATELY SO. The 2026 regime is real and I found named provenance: Gilead/Arcellx, announced February 2026, ~$7.8bn for anito-cel, a late-stage CAR-T with a US decision due December 2026; J&J/Firefly Bio $1bn; five in-vivo cell-therapy acquisitions totalling over $7.3bn between March 2025 and February 2026. But the lens conditions on "pivotal data IN HAND or near approval," and Immatics is neither — SUPRAME has not read out, and Arcellx carried registrational data plus a Kite partnership when Gilead bid. Anzu-cel post-win would be the only randomised-controlled solid-tumour TCR-T asset in existence, which is genuine strategic scarcity, and plausible acquirers are Gilead (Kite cell-therapy infrastructure, explicitly buying late-stage cell therapy) and Merck & Co (melanoma franchise adjacency). Bristol Myers Squibb is the obvious name and the WEAKEST one: it handed IMA401 back effective 12-Dec-2024, so the large-pharma validation on the bispecific franchise is already gone. Conclusion: the takeout leg is undated optionality that becomes live only AFTER a SUPRAME win, at which point it is embedded in the re-rate — it is not a milestone, it does not extend or substitute for one, and it does not lift $14.00 today. It is, however, where the board's $20 was implicitly coming from; a post-win takeout at a 40-60% premium to standalone reaches $19-22, which is a CONDITIONAL CAP, not fair value.

5) INSTRUMENT NOTE (fact, not a trade view): the board's own instrument line already flags that options carry a full 9-12 month binary IV load. That was written when the binary was expected to resolve in 2026; after the slip the option path now spans roughly four quarters MORE than the board assumed. Tradeability is the CRO's call — recording the fact only.

VNDA.thesis_summary: Vanda ($5.23, 60.1M sh, $315M cap) carries a hard, forward-dated FDA binary: the imsidolimab (anti-IL-36R mAb) BLA for generalized pustular psoriasis, PDUFA target action date 2026-12-12, accepted for filing 2026-02-25. The pivotal record is clean and public — GEMINI-1 met its primary endpoint (53.3% vs 13.3% GPPPGA 0/1 at wk4, p=0.0131), published in NEJM Evidence 2026-04-28, with orphan designation in the US, EU (2026-07-16) and Japan (2026-05-27). The event is idiosyncratic (a single agency decision on its own dossier) and unfired. It sits on top of a real commercial base — 2026 revenue guided $240-290M, Fanapt +26% in Q1 — that the market currently values at roughly 0.47x sales after netting cash, so very little imsidolimab value is embedded in the tape. The offsetting fact is a balance sheet running down fast: cash+ST investments fell $61.5M in Q1-26 alone, to $202.3M, and management has guided 2026 burn above 2025's.
VNDA.kill_risk: Financing gap ahead of the event. Net cash/share has collapsed from the ~$6.75 the board itself cited in 2024 when rejecting Cycle Pharma's $8.00 cash bid, to $3.37 at 2026-03-31 — Q1-26 alone consumed $61.5M of cash+ST investments, and management guided 2026 burn above 2025. A registration statement went effective 2026-05-05 (EFFECT, CIK 1347178), i.e. the shelf is armed. An equity raise between the 2026-08-05 Q2 print and the 2026-12-12 PDUFA would dilute the win leg before it pays, and every quarter of burn erodes the downside floor by roughly $0.58/sh of net cash. Second, independent risk: imsidolimab is Vanda's FIRST biologic BLA, so CMC and pre-approval-inspection failure — the modal CRL cause and entirely invisible from the efficacy record above — is not covered by the strong GEMINI-1 result. The historical "Vanda always loses at FDA" bear case (Hetlioz jet-lag CRL 2026-01-08, tradipitant gastroparesis) is the weaker objection and I discount it: FDA approved BYSANTI on 2026-02-20 and NEREUS in 2026, two on-time wins this year.

The scan appears to have grabbed the next calendar event and mislabeled it as the approval decision. Q1-26 (3/31/26) balance sheet: cash $54.0M + ST inv $148.3M = $202.3M ($3.37/sh); LT inv $0.4M; total debt $13.1M (finance leases only, no funded debt). Net cash $189.6M = $3.15/sh. Current EV = 314.5 - 189.6 = $124.9M, i.e. 0.47x the $265M midpoint of 2026 revenue guidance ($240-290M incl. $10-30M NEREUS). The market is pricing the burn, not the revenue line.

BURN PATH (drives both legs). Cash+ST inv: Q2-25 $325.6M -> Q3-25 $293.8M (-31.8) -> Q4-25 $263.8M (-30.0) -> Q1-26 $202.3M (-61.5). Q1-26 doubled the 2025 run-rate; management guided 2026 burn above 2025. I mark Q2-Q4-26 at a normalized $35M/qtr (below Q1's print, since Fanapt/NEREUS/BYSANTI revenue is ramping): net cash at the PDUFA = 189.6 - 3(35) = $84.6M = $1.41/sh. Both legs below are marked to THAT figure, not to today's cash - a floor computed off 3/31 cash would be ~$1.75/sh too generous by December.

WIN LEG (approval 2026-12-12) = $8.90. Commercial base at 1.0x forward revenue, 2027E ~$300M -> $300M; plus imsidolimab GPP at $150M; plus net cash $84.6M = $534.6M / 60.1M sh = $8.89, call it $8.90. The $150M GPP mark is benchmarked to SPEVIGO (spesolimab, Boehringer) - the only approved GPP therapy and the SAME IL-36R mechanism, running roughly $150-250M globally. Imsidolimab arrives second into an ultra-rare indication (~3-5k diagnosed US patients), so I carry US peak at $80-120M and value it near 1.5x peak less launch risk. I did not underwrite the GLP-1-emesis (Thetis) or CMT2S (VCA-894A) options - both are early and undated.

LOSE LEG (CRL) = $3.60. Commercial base at a distressed 0.5x 2026 revenue (0.5 x $265M = $132.5M) + net cash $84.6M = $217.1M / 60.1M = $3.61. Cross-check: the observed max-fear print this cycle is the $4.14 52wk low, set into the 2026-01-08 Hetlioz jet-lag CRL and the securities-investigation wave (Pomerantz, Levi & Korsinsky). My $3.60 sits BELOW that print deliberately - the January low was struck against a materially fatter cash balance, so the old floor is stale-HIGH here, the opposite of the usual XBI-at-highs caution.

R:R AND EV. Upside 8.90 - 5.23 = $3.67; downside 5.23 - 3.60 = $1.63; R:R = 2.25:1. EV = 0.75(8.90) + 0.25(3.60) = $7.58, or +45% vs spot.

TAKEOUT LENS - APPLIED AND REJECTED, does NOT lift the win leg. Vanda has demonstrated acquirer interest: Future Pak bid $7.25-7.75/sh (March and May 2024, latter plus CVRs) and Cycle Pharma bid $8.00/sh cash valuing Vanda at ~$466M. All were rejected unanimously; Vanda adopted a poison-pill shareholder rights plan. Three reasons I refuse to mark those comps into fair value: (1) the board's own rejection rationale was that $7.25-7.75 was "a mere 7-15% premium to Vanda's cash balance of approximately $6.75 per share" - that cash balance is now $3.37/sh, so the arithmetic underpinning those bids is gone, and the bids are stale by two years; (2) founder-CEO Polymeropoulos plus the pill make the board a demonstrated structural blocker, not a seller; (3) the 2026 record M&A tape (37 biotechs >=$1B YTD, $216B) is a LATE-STAGE, commercially-ready, >=$1B-asset phenomenon - a $315M cap whose lead asset is second-to-market behind an entrenched Boehringer product is not the scarce asset that regime is bidding for. Takeout is undated optionality only; per mandate it creates no milestone and I have not extended one.

ONE FLAG FOR THE CRO: FMP shows a $21 "consensus" price target, but targetHigh = targetLow = targetMedian = $21, i.e. a single analyst. It is 4x spot and ~2.4x my approval-leg number. Treat it as one datapoint, not a consensus - it is probably why the name is screening as edge_grade H, and it is not defensible from the live record.

ALVO.thesis_summary: Alvotech resubmitted US BLAs for AVT05 (Simponi/Simponi Aria biosimilar) and AVT06 (Eylea 2mg biosimilar) on 2026-06-04 after the Jan-2026 facility-driven CRLs; the company states it "expects the FDA to conduct a six-month review," clocking an approval decision to roughly 2026-12-04. The defect that caused the CRLs was site-specific (deficiencies from the July-2025 Reykjavik pre-license inspection), and on 2026-07-29 the FDA closed its May-2026 re-inspection of that same facility as Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) - i.e. no OAI, no approval-withholding classification. That is the single gating condition being cleared while the review clock runs, and it post-dates the board's 2026-06-08 valuation. Teva commercializes both assets. The equity is a thin stub over ~$1.53B debt and negative book equity (-$282M), so the December decision is genuinely binary at the equity level.
ALVO.kill_risk: The Q2 print on 2026-08-19 can spend the position before the catalyst ever resolves. Consensus Q2 revenue is $103M; with Q1 at $105.9M, H1 lands near $209M against unchanged FY guidance of $650-700M, requiring $441-491M in H2 - a 2.1-2.3x step-up off the H1 run-rate. A guidance cut re-rates the stub on leverage and cash burn, not on FDA odds, and there is precedent: the Jan-2026 CRL was accompanied by a slashed revenue guide and a 58% cut to adjusted EBITDA. The financing pattern corroborates stress rather than strength - $165M of equity issued at $3.75 (closed 06-17) followed by a $75M GoldenTree term loan just two weeks later (07-01). Separately, Celtic Lux (the founder vehicle) pledged 88,940,619 shares plus 7,007,321 depository receipts on 2026-06-26, ten days after buying 10.13M shares at $3.75; a pledged ~28% of the share count against a stock already near its 52-week low is a forced-sale vector that can break the $2.40 floor for reasons unrelated to the BLAs. Also note the December date is derived, not FDA-published (see dossier_note).

Board dossier was struck 2026-06-08, four days after the resubmission, and never picked up the clock.

ALVO.dossier_note:
MILESTONE DERIVATION - READ THIS BEFORE SIZING. The 2026-12-04 date is INFERRED, not published. I fetched both primary releases: the 06-04 resubmission PR says only "The company expects the FDA to conduct a six-month review of the resubmitted applications, consistent with the applicable regulatory timelines" and states NO target action date; the 07-29 VAI release also gives no timeline (CEO Lisa Graver: "We continue to work with the FDA to advance our recent Biologics Licence Applications towards approval"). The BsUFA Class 2 clock runs from FDA RECEIPT, not the announcement date, and FDA never publicly confirmed the resubmission class. Treat the milestone as a Nov-2026-to-Jan-2027 window centred on Dec 4, not a hard day-certain print. It is PENDING_HARD because the six-month statutory clock is binding, not because the day is known.

SCOPE - only AVT05 and AVT06 are on this clock. AVT03 (denosumab, Prolia/Xgeva) is NOT: the 06-04 PR states Dr. Reddy's "as applicant, is responsible for the U.S. regulatory submission," so its resubmission is separate and un-clocked. AVT16 (Entyvio biosimilar) had its BLA ACCEPTED 2026-06-08, a first-cycle review landing ~Q1-Q2 2027 - a later, separate event. Do not let the CRO fold AVT03/AVT16 into the December binary.

ARITHMETIC. The board's set reproduces exactly at the live price, so the errors are inputs, not math: win 6.00 / lose 2.75 / p 0.65 from 3.79 gives up +58.3%, down -27.4%, R:R 2.12, EV +28.3% - byte-matching the board's payoff 2.12 and ev_pct 0.283. Corrected set: win 5.70 / lose 2.40 / p 0.72 gives up +50.4%, down -36.7%, R:R 1.37, EV +26.0%. Dilution bridge for the target: 293.0M shares (Q1) -> 338.2M today = +45.2M at $3.75; 45.2M x ($6.00-$3.75) = $102M / 338.2M = $0.30/sh; $6.00 - $0.30 = $5.70. Cross-check on the raise: 26,066,667 public x $3.75 = $97.8M, plus Celtic Lux 10,133,333 x $3.75 = $38.0M, plus ~$29M residual private placement = ~$165M aggregate as announced, ~44M shares - reconciles with the 45.2M implied by market cap. MARKET-IMPLIED PROBABILITY: at my two legs the tape is paying (3.79-2.40)/(5.70-2.40) = 42%. That 42% vs my 72% IS the entire edge - there is no valuation cushion underneath it. At the board's legs the implied number was 32%.

TAKEOUT LENS - NO LIFT APPLIED, and I want that on the record. ALVO is bio/pharma by label but does not fit the 2026 takeout regime, which is bidding clean late-stage/commercially-ready ASSETS. Alvotech is a levered manufacturing PLATFORM: $1.53B total debt (Q1 $1.457B + the $75M 07-01 GoldenTree term loan), negative book equity of -$282M, and its two lead US assets are already economically committed to Teva on commercialization. Logical strategics (Teva, Dr. Reddy's, Sandoz, Fresenius Kabi) are existing partners who get the economics without the balance sheet. I found NO named comparable takeout with date and value that would support a higher win leg, so per the provenance rule the target stays at $5.70. No milestone was created or extended from takeout speculation.

XBI CAVEAT CUTS THE OTHER WAY HERE. The standing warning - that a 5-year-high XBI makes market-implied win probabilities rich and old max-fear floors stale-low - does NOT apply to this name. ALVO has not participated: -64% over the trailing year, $3.79 against a 52-week range of $2.94-$9.25, 50-day $3.55 vs 200-day $4.47, and it just traded -8.0% on the session. This is an idiosyncratically broken name inside a strong tape, which is why a 42% market-implied probability is available at all - but it also means the $2.94 low is RECENT, not stale, and there is no sector bid propping the downside leg.

SKEPTIC PASS. Load-bearing claim tested: "VAI clears the path, so the December decision approves." Strongest refutation I can mount from the live record - VAI is not an approval commitment. The FDA still issued a Form 483 at the close of the May-2026 inspection, and VAI explicitly means objectionable conditions were FOUND but did not warrant regulatory action; it removes the site as a blocker without speaking to product-specific review issues in either BLA. Sequencing is favourable (resubmitted 06-04, inspection closed 07-29, decision ~Dec) but the company has now missed on this exact axis once, and Hagens Berman is investigating the adequacy of its manufacturing and regulatory-status disclosures. I held the lift to +7pp (0.65 -> 0.72) rather than the +10-15pp a clean facility-only read would justify. The residual risk that actually threatens the trade is not the FDA, though - it is the 08-19 Q2 print and the pledged founder stake; both are in kill_risk and both can resolve against the position months before the catalyst does.

IFF.thesis_summary: Signed, binding sale of IFF's Food Ingredients disposal group to CVC Capital Partners for ~$4.3bn EV / ~$3.8bn net cash proceeds, agreement dated 28 May 2026, guided to close by end of Q2 2027, outside date 28 May 2027, no financing condition, IFF retains an ~10% minority stake. The event is real, dated, unfired and idiosyncratic. Asset carries FDA Breakthrough Therapy (Jan 2026), RMAT, and ODD in the US and EU; there is no approved CAR-T in AL amyloidosis. Balance sheet is funded through the event: ~$231M cash+investments post the 2026-05-22 $150M raise (net $140.65M), runway guided to mid-2028, so the readout is not a financing event. The trade is binary on a readout the company controls, not on the tape. The overhang is governance, not efficacy: on 2026-07-20 IMMX terminated the CMO hired in March 2026 ("Richard Graydon") after press reports identified him as Ronald Fischer, a Rhode Island fugitive of ~20 years arrested the prior week; the 8-K states the termination was for reasons unrelated to his activities at the company and no material business effect given his short tenure, but five plaintiffs' firms opened securities investigations within ten days and the stock is ~30% off its $12.14 52-week high.

TMC.thesis_summary: TMC the metals company is a pre-revenue deep-sea polymetallic-nodule developer, NOT a biotech. The resolving event is NOAA's grant or denial of the consolidated TMC USA-A exploration licence plus commercial recovery permit under the Deep Seabed Hard Mineral Resources Act — an idiosyncratic, discretionary US federal grant that resolves on its own administrative record rather than on the tape. The application was found in full compliance (28 Apr 2026) and was published in the Federal Register on 19 Aug 2026 (FR 2026-16869), with a virtual public hearing 13 Oct 2026 and written comments closing 19 Oct 2026; a separate NOI to prepare an EIS for the lesser USA-B exploration licence published 17 Aug 2026 (FR 2026-16722). The event is real, forward and unfired, but it has SLIPPED: management's April-2026 language that the process would conclude before end-Q1-2027 was replaced on the 13 Aug 2026 Q2 call by "continues to expect the permit in advance of targeted Q4 2027 offshore collection system commissioning" — i.e. the decision is now undated by the company's own disclosure, and TMC's 19 Aug 2026 release affirms "the absence of any mandatory statutory deadline under DSHMRA for completion of NOAA's review". Valuation is a two-legged permit binary against a balance sheet with negative book equity (−$27.4m), $98.7m cash, $208.3m total liabilities and an active ATM. On my re-derivation the market is roughly efficiently priced: win-leg $6.80, lose-leg $1.75, breakeven grant probability 53.3% against a live $4.44.
TMC.dated_milestone: Procedural dates only, all Federal-Register-verified: 16 Sep 2026 USA-B EIS scoping comments close (FR 2026-16722, pub. 17 Aug 2026); 13 Oct 2026 NOAA virtual public hearing on the consolidated USA-A application, 3-5pm ET; 19 Oct 2026 written comments close (FR 2026-16869, pub. 19 Aug 2026). The resolving event — NOAA's grant or denial of the USA-A commercial recovery permit — carries NO date and no statutory deadline; management now guides only to "in advance of targeted Q4 2027" commissioning.
TMC.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that this is a live, bounded, forward event. It largely refutes on the live record. The EIS for the USA-A COMMERCIAL RECOVERY permit — the only instrument that authorises mining — has not been noticed; the single NOI on file (FR 2026-16722, 17 Aug 2026) covers the USA-B EXPLORATION licence, a different area and a lesser instrument. A full EIS must still be drafted, opened for comment and finalised before any permit can issue, and 15 CFR part 971 subpart C binds NOAA only to "endeavor" to certify within 100 days — a soft target on the completeness step, with nothing at all governing grant or denial. October 2026 therefore delivers a hearing, a comment close and an administrative certification, none of which is a probability update on issuance. Meanwhile the claim on the same NAV is being diluted continuously: 433,726,201 shares at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 release) rising to roughly 441.1m on the 13 Aug 10-Q cover, i.e. the ATM ran straight through the August rally, against negative book equity and ~$0.22 of cash per share under a $4.44 quote. An undated discretionary grant whose governing environmental review has not started, financed by a live ATM, can drift for years while the share count grows — the denominator moves and the clock does not. XRN.thesis_summary: Chiron Real Estate (NYSE: XRN, ex-Global Medical REIT, 13.235M shares, $35.27) is mid-way through a self-directed recapitalization that converts a legacy net-lease medical-office book into a senior-housing operating (SHOP) platform. Announced 2026-05-06: $425M of Silverstone SHOP communities, a $100M delayed-draw convertible perpetual preferred led by Maewyn Capital, ~$200M of asset sales, a new debt facility, a 36% monthly dividend cut to $0.16, and withdrawal of 2026 guidance. Two legs have already fired: The Landing + The Riviera closed 2026-06-01 for $249M, and seven IRFs were recapitalized into an 85/15 JV with a US public pension fund at a $217M aggregate valuation on 2026-06-30. What remains forward is the third community, The Pinnacle North Bethesda, at ~$176M, company-guided to close October 2026 (broadened to Q4 2026 in the 06-01 release), plus the balance of the ~$200M disposition program. The equity is a sum-of-parts on depreciated real estate: management's own disclosure that the $249M of SHOP equals ~14% of the portfolio by gross real estate assets implies ~$1.78B of gross cost against $1.238B of depreciated assets and $668.6M of net debt, so roughly $540M (~$41/share) of accumulated depreciation sits between carrying value and cost. The market caps the legacy book at ~76% of gross cost; marking it at 85% and holding the two 2026 transacted assets at their own arms-length prices gets to ~$44/share. This is a NAV-discount repositioning story with a soft-dated deal close, not a hard binary event.
XRN.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the legacy net-lease medical book is worth materially more than its depreciated carrying value, and the live record pushes back hard. (1) The one completed disposition was structured as an 85/15 JV RECAPITALIZATION rather than an outright sale - that is what issuers do when an outright bid will not clear their mark; the $217M is a headline gross asset valuation, and because I cannot see JV-level debt from the record, my $32.6M mark on the retained 15% (0.15 x $217M) OVERSTATES the retained equity if the JV is levered, which it almost certainly is. (2) The ~$540M of accumulated depreciation on a physician-practice MOB book is partly real economic obsolescence, not purely an accounting artifact, and 2026 MOB cap rates sit above the 2016-2022 acquisition cap rates - so gross cost is a ceiling, not a proxy for market value. At 75% of gross cost the SoP prints $34.22, i.e. the entire discount vanishes and the market is simply right. (3) The 36% dividend cut is a direct issuer signal that the legacy book's cash generation did not support the prior payout. (4) The pivot swaps contractual net-lease income for operating risk with 2026 guidance withdrawn and Q2 consensus at -$0.235 EPS; the first print carrying SHOP economics lands 2026-08-05 AMC, one day out and entirely unpriced by this dossier. (5) The Maewyn convertible perpetual preferred ranks ahead of the common AND converts, so it clips the top of any NAV re-rating. (6) I could not reconstruct a cap-rate NAV independently: FMP's REIT line mapping is internally contradictory (Q1-26 EBITDA + G&A annualizes to ~$115M of NOI, while revenue less implied property opex annualizes to ~$56M - a 2x spread), and the SEC 10-Q and Q1 8-K exhibits returned HTTP 403, so the SoP rests on the company's own 14%/25% portfolio-mix statistic rather than on verified NOI.

No covenant breach, no index deletion, no court- or regulator-ordered divestiture, and the 2026-07-31 filing is a SC 13G (passive), not a 13D, so no activist process either. The disposition program is self-directed capital recycling announced by management on 2026-05-06 to fund the SHOP pivot, and the company is simultaneously HIRING for it (COO, Chief Development Officer/Head of Seniors Housing, and CIO appointed 2026-07-14 and 2026-08-03 with NYSE 303A.08 inducement awards) - that is a build-out, not a forced wind-down. VALUATION - SoP, arithmetic. All axes are mine; the board emitted nulls. Anchor is the company's own portfolio-mix disclosure in the 2026-06-01 release: the $249M of closed SHOP equals ~14% of the portfolio by gross real estate assets, so gross real estate cost = 249 / 0.14 = $1,778.6M. Cross-check against the same release's pro forma statement that Pinnacle plus ~$200M of sales takes SHOP to ~25%: (249 + 176) / (1,778.6 + 176 - 200) = 425 / 1,754.6 = 24.2%. Consistent, so the $1.78B gross figure is reliable. Against $1,238.0M of depreciated total assets at 2026-03-31, that implies ~$540M (~$41/share) of accumulated depreciation between carrying value and cost - the NAV wedge.

Components, pro forma post-06-30: (a) SHOP Landing + Riviera at their own 2026-06-01 arms-length price, $249M; (b) retained 15% of the IRF JV at the pension fund's own 2026-06-30 mark, 0.15 x 217 = $32.6M; (c) legacy net-lease medical book at gross cost 1,778.6 - 249 - 217 = $1,313M, marked at 85% of cost = $1,116M to reflect 2026 MOB cap rates sitting above the 2016-2022 acquisition cap rates. GAV = 249 + 32.6 + 1,116 = $1,397.2M. Less net debt $668.6M, preferred at carrying $124.1M, minority interest $20.4M = $584.1M common equity / 13.235M shares = $44.13, taken as fair_value_target $44.00 (+24.8% vs $35.27). Net debt is held at the 2026-03-31 figure because the pro forma legs roughly offset ($249M out for SHOP against ~$184M gross in from the 85% JV sale) and the JV-level debt is not visible in the record.

Sensitivity on the only free variable, the legacy mark: 90% of cost = $49.09/share; 85% = $44.13; 75% = $34.22. At 75% the discount disappears entirely - the market's current $35.27 is capitalizing the legacy book at ~76% of gross cost. That single assumption carries the whole thesis, which is why it is the kill_risk.

R:R at these axes is roughly 1.3:1 - thin for an event sleeve.

FMP's REIT line mapping is self-contradictory - Q1-26 EBITDA $23.714M plus G&A $5.089M annualizes to ~$115M of NOI, while revenue $38.064M less implied property opex ($38.904M cost of revenue - $14.827M D&A = $24.08M) annualizes to only ~$56M. There is no US filing on file, and the only pending regulator action is a European Commission decision whose applicant/MAH is A. Menarini International Licensing S.A. — NAMS's EU economics are milestone-plus-royalty, not direct. The event that actually resolves the priced spread is the PREVAIL cardiovascular outcomes trial (9,500+ patients, enrolled April 2024): per the company's 2026-08-05 release the interim analysis is planned for 4Q2026 with the RESULT expected 1Q2027, and completion end-2027 if not stopped early. RUBENS (~300 patients, T2D/metabolic syndrome, topline by year-end 2026) is a label-enhancement readout, not the binary. The EC decision (statutory 67-day clock from the 23-24 July CHMP opinion, so ~2026-09-29) is ~99% concordant with a positive CHMP opinion and the marketing authorisation accrues to Menarini as applicant/MAH; RUBENS is a ~300-patient label extension. Underneath that: CETP is 0-for-4 in commercialised CV outcomes, obicetrapib's incremental LDL-C reduction sits on top of background statins, and Merck's Lipfendra (enlicitide, first oral PCSK9, FDA-approved 15 July 2026, up to ~60% LDL-C reduction) now occupies the exact US oral add-on slot obicetrapib cannot reach before roughly 2029 with no NDA filed. My $52 win leg is itself borrowed authority — it is a 12-month risk-adjusted street consensus used as a pure-win value, which cuts both ways (it understates a clean CVOT win and overstates a win that arrives three years second into an occupied US market).

PVLA.thesis_summary: Palvella Therapeutics (Wayne PA, 14.34M shares, $2.02B cap) has one asset that matters: QTORIN 3.9% rapamycin anhydrous gel for microcystic lymphatic malformations (mLM), a rare vascular malformation with ~30,000 diagnosed US patients and ZERO FDA-approved therapies. The pivotal event already fired: Phase 3 SELVA read out positive 2026-02-24 (n=49 ITT, mean +2.13 on the mLM-IGA at Week 24, p<0.001; key secondary and all four additional secondaries also p<0.001), and the stock is up ~620% off the $36 low. What is STILL unfired is the regulatory conversion: FDA granted rolling review 2026-06-22, Palvella submitted the first NDA module 2026-06-29, and guides to COMPLETING the 505(b)(2) NDA in 2H 2026 with potential US approval and launch in 1H 2027. Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track are in hand; $261.9M cash at 3/31/26 after the upsized $230M February raise fully funds submission, launch build-out, and the 2H26 Phase 3 start in cutaneous venous malformations (75,000 US patients) plus the Phase 2 LOTU angiokeratoma readout (2H 2027). The remaining edge is therefore regulatory/commercial conversion of an already-de-risked efficacy package, not a data event - and the milestone is a guided half-year window, not a binding date.
PVLA.kill_risk: SELVA is a SINGLE-ARM, BASELINE-CONTROLLED Phase 3 whose primary endpoint is an unblinded clinician-rated global assessment (mLM-IGA). There is no vehicle arm, so neither placebo/attention effect nor natural fluctuation of a chronic lesional disease is quantified, and the assessor was not blinded to treatment. That is exactly the package FDA can meet with a CRL demanding a controlled confirmatory trial - which would reset the timeline 2-3 years and take the equity to roughly the downside floor. Compounding it: the 2043-protected IP and $100-200k/yr pricing frame collide with compounded topical sirolimus, already used off-label at vascular-anomaly centers, so payer step-edits could cap real uptake well below the ">$1B US peak" bull frame even on approval. Secondary residual: the near-term event is only NDA COMPLETION inside an undated 2H26 window - a slip into 2027 is a de-rating (roughly the $109 200-day / pre-June levels) without any thesis break, so the position can bleed on timing alone with no falsifying news.

The arrangement-agreement outside date is 2026-11-01; management's 2026-07-29 language is "still targeting closing for the latter part of 2026." Valuation is a pro-forma EV/EBITDA sum-of-parts, not a spread. Re-derived from filed numbers: pro-forma Adj EBITDA C$2,865M (GFL FY26 guidance C$2,290M raised 07-29 + SECURE C$550M reaffirmed at the top of C$520-550M on 07-29 + C$25M disclosed run-rate synergies), pro-forma net debt C$11,495M, 434.1M shares, giving US$50.50 at a generous 14.6x peer anchor. The debate record's US$57 does not survive: it rested on a 9-10x purchase multiple that appears in no company document — GFL's own 2026-04-13 deck puts the deal at ~11.9x 2026E and ~11x post-synergy against a GFL standalone ~13.1x, so this is a modest currency arbitrage, not three to four turns. The separate take-private process (special committee confirmed 2026-07-29, reported level ~US$50) is undated optionality that caps at roughly the same number as the fundamental target, with a founder holding 25%+ of the vote who says he will roll 100% of his equity — it supports the floor more than it lifts the ceiling.
GFL.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that Competition Bureau clearance is close to a formality — which is exactly what the live tape encodes: SECURE trades C$24.18 against a mark-to-market mixed-election value of C$24.227 at GFL.TO C$57.44, a 0.19% discount, i.e. essentially zero deal risk priced. The live record refutes that complacency. This same regulator litigated SECURE's last major merger in this exact market — the Commissioner proved a substantial lessening of competition in 136 of 143 markets in SECURE/Tervita, the Tribunal ordered divestiture of 29 facilities (2023-03), the Federal Court of Appeal upheld it, and the Supreme Court denied leave (2024-02) — and the Bureau separately challenged GFL's own Terrapure acquisition in 2021. The review has now run ~3.8 months against Dovigi's own 3-5 month estimate, consistent with a deep supplementary-information-request process rather than an early no-action letter. A remedy package that carves facilities out of SECURE would cut both the C$550M EBITDA and the C$25M synergy and drops the target below US$50 while the shares carry the full 11.9x purchase price. Second residual: even on clean clearance the win requires a re-rate toward mid-teens peers, which my own build says is unearned — pro-forma leverage lands at 4.0x on the Adj EBITDA basis (3.9x on management's Run-Rate convention) versus the guided "low-to-mid 3s," so GFL's discount to WM/RSG/WCN is arguably a fair charge for balance-sheet and oilfield-waste cyclicality, not a closable gap. Third: US$50.50 IS the sell-side consensus (US$50.95 mean, US$52.00 median) — there is no differentiated upside in this number, and because GFL is the acquirer there is no contractual backstop, no break fee receivable in a regulatory block, and GFL owes up to C$20M in expense reimbursement.

ASPI.thesis_summary: Sum-of-the-parts on a four-legged advanced-materials holdco (Renergen helium/LNG, radiopharmacy+enriched isotopes, Quantum Leap Energy nuclear fuels, net cash), where the resolving event is NOT the spin the board recorded. There is no QLE distribution and no record date: the 10-Q filed 14 Aug 2026 still says "a to-be-determined future record date," the same words used in 2024 and 2025. The live, dated, binding corporate event is a different transaction — the Noble Africa / ENDRA reverse merger (Nasdaq: NOBA), signed 25 Jun 2026, with a contractual outside termination date of 24 Dec 2026 — and it pays ASPI holders nothing: ASPI retains ~89-90% of Noble, so there is no distribution and therefore no index-flow mechanism at all. What the deal does deliver is a price: a $50m concurrent subscription at $6.57/unit that marks the Renergen stake ASPI already owns. That mark, taken as struck, supports a SoP of ~$4.50 against a broken-deal floor of ~$2.80. From $3.89 that is +16% versus -28%, reward/risk ~0.56 — below 1:1, and the inverse of the board's 1.99.
ASPI.kill_risk: The whole win leg rests on one number — $6.57 per Noble unit — and that number is thin, interested, and conditional. Of the ~$50m subscription, ASPI itself takes 3,054,185 Class B Units (~$20.07m) and ASPI insiders (Mann $500,003, Ryan $100,002, Ainscow $100,002, Moore $49,998) take a further ~$0.75m, leaving only ~$29.4m of genuinely third-party money — about 7% of the 63.1m units — setting the price for the other ~93%. It marks Renergen equity at 55.5m x $6.57 = $364.6m, roughly 1.9x the $192.96m purchase-accounting carrying value of the same natural gas properties on the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, and a large multiple of the <=14.27m ASPI shares ASPI paid for 100% of Renergen only seven months earlier (Jan 2026). It was struck on 25 Jun 2026 with ASPI at $6.35; ASPI is $3.89 today, a 39% de-rating of the same complex. And it only prints if the Merger closes — which requires an S-4 that, as of 25 Aug 2026, does not exist. Secondary leaks on the floor: the S-3ASR filed 16 Jul 2026 makes 23,160,682 shares (15.1% of shares out) freely resalable with no lockup while the 10-Q says the company "anticipates it will need to continue to raise capital"; and the fifth addendum to the ASPI Term Loan Facility, to be signed at or prior to Closing, lets ASPI lend Renergen up to $200m — a claim on the very cash line the floor credits.

SBGI.thesis_summary: Sinclair is a ~5.8x-levered broadcast stub ($1.01B equity on $4.19B gross debt) trading at roughly 6.1x normalized EBITDA, with two live-but-undated corporate-action legs: (1) the Aug-2025 board-authorized dual-track strategic review of the Broadcast business, and (2) a separation of Sinclair Ventures ($489M cash + $340M carried investments) via spin/split. The dated leg that the board dossier's edge rested on has already fired: the FCC adopted the order eliminating the 39% national ownership cap on 2026-08-06 (2-1), and the stock did not re-rate on it ($14.51 today vs a $14.10 50-day average). What remains is an undated consolidation process. Management reaffirmed intent on the 2026-08-05 call ("well prepared to participate in value-creating consolidation", the repeal "de-risks those opportunities"), but there is no Form 10 for Ventures on EDGAR, no 8-K Item 1.01, and no signed control transaction — 13 months after the review was announced. The equity is therefore a cheap levered call on a broadcast control transaction, not a dated event trade: SoP marks fair value near $21 at a 6.75x consolidation comp, against a de-rate floor near $9. WATCH-grade; the asymmetry is real but the trigger is absent.
SBGI.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the ~$6.50/share gap between spot and SoP is a discount waiting on a transaction. The live record argues it is instead the correct price for a terminal-decline asset carrying 5.8x leverage, and three facts support that reading. First, the Smith family's supervoting Class B stock makes SBGI effectively un-takeoverable and un-pressurable — no activist or hostile bidder can force realization, and the family has consistently chosen to be the buyer, not the seller. Second, the last capital-allocation move made under exactly this thesis destroyed value: Sinclair accumulated 9.9% of Scripps and bid $7/share in December 2025; the board unanimously rejected it and SSP now trades at $3.32, marking that stake roughly 50%+ below the bid Sinclair itself put on the table. Third, and most damaging, the market paid nothing for the cap repeal — the single event the whole consolidation case waited on cleared on 2026-08-06 and SBGI is 3% above its 50-day average and 19% below its 52-week high, while SSP (-38% from high), GTN and NXST all sit below their 200-day averages. If the repeal did not re-rate the group, the SoP is not being suppressed by regulation; it is being discounted for secular erosion, and the entire target rests on a multiple assertion (each 0.5 turn is ~$5.00/share) rather than on any observable transaction.

SBGI.dossier_note:
VALUATION ARITHMETIC (all inputs from the 10-Q filed 2026-08-05 for the period ended 2026-06-30, the Q2 call, and live quotes on 2026-08-25).

Balance sheet, 6/30/26: cash $604M; total debt $4,192M (incl. $133M finance leases); net debt $3,588M; long-term investments $340M. Q2 call: $489M of the cash sits AT VENTURES, Ventures threw off $19M of distributions in the quarter, total debt ~$4.1B, STG net leverage 5.2x.

Normalized EBITDA base. Two independent derivations. (a) Guidance: FY26 adjusted EBITDA raised at Q2 from $700-740M to $730-760M — but 2026 is a political year, so the midpoint $745M is cycle-peak, not normalized; a non-political 2027 lands materially lower, so a two-year average sits near $660-680M. (b) Covenant back-solve: STG cash = $604M total - $489M Ventures = $115M, so STG net debt = $4,192M - $115M = $4,077M; at the disclosed 5.2x trailing-average leverage that implies ~$784M of STG-only covenant EBITDA (which excludes corporate drag and includes add-backs). I take $700M as the normalized consolidated base — between the two derivations and deliberately below the political-year guide.

EV-to-equity bridge (constant across cases): + STG cash $115M + Ventures cash $489M + Ventures carried investments $340M - total debt $4,192M = -$3,248M. Equity = (multiple x $700M) - $3,248M, over 69.9M shares.

  5.5x -> $3,850M - $3,248M = $602M  -> $8.61/sh
  6.0x -> $4,200M - $3,248M = $952M  -> $13.62/sh
  6.09x = today's $14.51 (i.e. the market is paying ~6.1x)
  6.75x -> $4,725M - $3,248M = $1,477M -> $21.13/sh   [fair_value_target, rounded $21]
  7.00x -> $4,900M - $3,248M = $1,652M -> $23.63/sh

Sensitivity that dominates everything: each 0.5 turn of multiple = $350M = $5.01/share, i.e. ~35% of the equity. This is a multiple bet with a broadcast asset attached, and the CRO should size it as such.

Why 6.75x for the win leg: it is the pre-synergy zone at which the announced broadcast control transactions of this cycle have been struck, and it is where the SoP realizes only if a transaction actually happens. It is a CONDITIONAL cap, not fair value in the absence of a deal — analogous to a deck-price mark. The unconditional, no-transaction mark is roughly where it trades today.

Downside floor $9.00: 5.5x on $700M gives $8.61 mechanically; I round to $9.00. Cross-check: the 52-week low is $12.46 and the stock has not printed below that in a year, so $9.00 requires a genuine de-rate (secular acceleration, a failed/aborted review, or leverage stress into a non-political 2027 when EBITDA steps down and 5.8x gross leverage becomes 6.5x+). I am NOT using $12.46 as the floor because the observed low predates the fired catalyst and understates the leverage math.

Ventures marks. The $340M of carried long-term investments is down from $525M at 3/31/26 — a $185M sequential write-down/realization in one quarter, which is itself a caution on how the Ventures pool marks in a spin. The Scripps stake is inside this: 9.9% of SSP at a $264M market cap is only ~$26M, immaterial to the SoP, but it is marked far below the $7/share Sinclair itself bid in December 2025 (SSP is $3.32 today).

CATALYST LEDGER, corrected.
FIRED 2026-08-06: FCC adopted the Report and Order (FCC 26-53) eliminating the 39% national audience-reach cap, 2-1, Gomez dissenting; replaced with case-by-case review. Sinclair issued a same-day statement commending it. Ripley on the 8/5 call: the rule enters the Federal Register ~30 days after adoption, enabling transactions shortly thereafter. This is administrative effectiveness of a decided matter — the edge is spent, and the tape agrees: SBGI is $14.51 against a $14.10 50-day average and a $14.65 200-day average. The single event the thesis waited on produced no re-rating.
STILL PENDING, UNDATED: the Aug-2025 dual-track review (Broadcast M&A + Ventures separation via spin/split/other). Verified absent from the primary record — EDGAR for CIK 0001971213 shows only a 10-Q and earnings 8-K (2026-08-05) and Forms 4 (2026-07-06, 2026-08-12); no Form 10, no Item 1.01 8-K. On the 8/5 call management gave no timing for a Ventures separation at all. A Form 10 alone puts any distribution four to six months out from a standing start, so index-flow mechanics are not reachable in 2026 under any scenario.
NOT A MILESTONE, but worth the CRO's attention: Scripps' limited-duration rights plan (adopted days after Sinclair's approach, ~2025-11-26) lapses on its one-year term around 2026-11-26, at which point Sinclair's 9.9% position is no longer capped by the pill. That is optionality on a re-approach, undated and third-party-controlled — it does not create a milestone and I have not treated it as one.

M&A LENS (not the biotech takeout lens — this is not a bio/pharma name, and the deck-mark gate does not apply either; no commodity price deck underlies the target). SBGI as a TARGET is close to unbuyable: the Smith family's supervoting Class B control means no transaction happens without family consent, which removes the usual takeout floor under the equity. SBGI as an ACQUIRER is the live path, and it consumes cash rather than realizing SoP — the Scripps campaign is the worked example, and it is currently a loss. Plausible counterparties named by management only generically ("counterparties that we are interested in"); the only one with a public record is Scripps, whose board unanimously rejected $622M / $7 per share on 2025-12-16.

Spectrum optionality, flagged not underwritten: Ripley put a floor of ">$2.50 per MHz-pop" on the spectrum, implying ~$4.1B portfolio-wide. That number exceeds the entire enterprise value and is a management assertion with no transaction behind it. I have deliberately excluded it from both the target and the floor — if the CRO wants it, it is an unpriced call option, not a valuation input.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE CRO: facts check out that this is a real, board-authorized, still-live process with a defensible ~$21 SoP against a $9 floor — but the dated leg is spent, no registration statement exists, and R:R is only ~1.18:1 from $14.51. Staging remains true.

BHF.thesis_summary: Signed all-cash merger: Aquarian Capital acquires Brighthouse at $70.00/share (~$4.1bn), agreement 6 Nov 2025, shareholder-adopted 12 Feb 2026, HSR expired. Every closing condition is satisfied or waived except acquisition-of-control approvals from the Delaware, New York and Massachusetts insurance regulators (plus FINRA for Brighthouse Securities). The deal did NOT close by its original 6 September 2026 outside date; the merger agreement's automatic extension has triggered because regulatory approvals were the sole unmet condition, pushing the termination right to 6 December 2026. No termination has been filed or announced. The binding gate is the Delaware Form A / Chapter 50 review of Brighthouse Life Insurance Company: as of the Department's 17 August 2026 statement it had retained outside actuaries, auditors and investigators, and had NOT noticed the statutorily required public hearing. At $53.58 the spread is 23.5% wide against a signed, shareholder-approved contract — the market is pricing roughly even odds of a Delaware denial or an Aquarian walk, not a capped arb.
BHF.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the Dec-6 extension keeps Aquarian on the hook at $70. It does not. Dec 6 is a termination RIGHT exercisable by EITHER party, not a self-executing deadline and not a commitment device — the extension bought calendar, not obligation. If Delaware signals it will condition approval on incremental capital at Brighthouse Reinsurance Company of Delaware, Aquarian can simply let 6 December pass and walk; nothing in the record establishes a reverse termination fee large enough to compel closing, and Aquarian's own financing backdrop sits under the same AM Best under-review-with-negative-implications umbrella (reaffirmed 29 July 2026). Second, my $45 floor assumes a break returns BHF to a peer-drift-marked unaffected price. A break caused by a Delaware DENIAL would not be a clean return: it stamps a public regulatory verdict on the affiliate-reinsurance capital structure that the Capitol Forum flagged on 7 August 2026, which is NEW adverse standalone information, and it simultaneously removes the private-capital bid pool for this balance sheet. In that specific branch the floor is $41 (~0.49x the $84.35 book, ~0.26x the $156.10 book ex-AOCI), which cuts R:R from 1.91 to 1.31 and lifts the market-implied close probability to 43.4% — within a point of my own 45% estimate, i.e. the edge goes to roughly zero. Third, the calendar itself is the quiet killer: with no hearing noticed and ~89 days left, a Delaware notice-hearing-decision sequence must begin by roughly mid-to-late October to land inside the window at all.

The merger agreement's outside date was 6 September 2026, automatically extended to 6 December 2026 because regulatory approvals were the only unmet condition (confirmed in the 6 Nov 2025 8-K terms and restated in the 5 Aug 2026 Q2 release). Dec 6 is the binding either-party termination right.

DRIVER. Kept as Deal_close_generic. Nuance: the true gate is neither antitrust (HSR is done) nor a foreign regulator — it is a domestic STATE insurance change-of-control consent, the Delaware Form A / Chapter 50 review of Brighthouse Life Insurance Company. No canonical tag covers that; Deal_close_generic is the least-wrong of the available set. The gating step is procedural and observable: Delaware must find the application complete, then notice a public hearing (published on the State Public Meeting Calendar and in the legal notices of the Delaware State News and the News Journal). Commissioner Trinidad Navarro's 17 Aug 2026 statement confirms outside actuaries, valuation experts, auditors, accountants, attorneys and investigators have been retained, that no hearing has been scheduled, and that the Department "cannot comment on the timing of any potential public hearing." Win leg, fair_value_target = $70.00. Contractual, all cash, no ticking fee, no common dividend accrual (BHF pays none). Board number CONFIRMED, not corrected.

(a) and (b) roughly offset, and (c) brackets the result. Floor $45.00, honest band $41-$48.
I am deliberately NOT taking the prior skeptic's $41 as the point estimate: that derivation deducted for a "de-rating through the auction year" while omitting the +10% peer drift over the same window, which is a one-sided mark. $41 is the Delaware-denial branch, carried in kill_risk.
Support underneath: book value $84.35/share, book ex-AOCI $156.10/share, combined RBC 430-450% (upper end of the company's 400-450% target), $0.9bn holding-company liquid assets, Q2 net income $956m ($16.53/diluted share), 57,508,193 shares out. A break also releases BHF from the merger agreement's interim operating covenants, restoring buyback capacity at roughly half of book — a real mechanical bid the pure-price analysis misses.

ARITHMETIC AT $53.58 (4 Sep 2026 close). Upside $16.42 (+30.6%); downside $8.58 (-16.0%); R:R = 16.42/8.58 = 1.91, versus the board's 9.22 which was purely (70.00-53.58)/(53.58-51.80). Market-implied close probability on my floor = (53.58-45.00)/(70.00-45.00) = 34.3%. Alternative joint solutions: at p=45% the implied floor is $40.15; at p=50%, $37.16. Either way the market has moved to genuinely doubting a signed, shareholder-approved, HSR-cleared all-cash deal.
Three-branch schedule to 6 Dec (89 days), win_prob = 0.45 on the $70 leg: 0.45 x $70.00 (closes) + 0.25 x $50.00 (still pending or re-extended past 6 Dec on a burnt calendar — worse-informed than today, so marked below spot) + 0.30 x $45.00 (Delaware denies or Aquarian walks) = $57.50, about +7.3% over 89 days against a 16% drawdown leg. Real but modest; on the $41 stress floor the same schedule gives $56.05, about +4.6%, which is noise.

WHAT THE TAPE ACTUALLY REPRICED. The blowout was not driven by an adverse regulatory ACTION. BHF closed $63.75 on 28 Jul and $61.86 on 5 Aug; it broke on 17 Aug (-5.04% to $55.74, 1.89m shares) and 18 Aug (-4.25% to $53.64, 2.17m shares) — on a Delaware press release that announced no decision and explicitly said no inference should be drawn. The bull case for the spread is that the market over-read a procedural non-statement. The bear case is that the Department's retention of investigators, and its silence with 89 days on the clock, is itself the signal.

Not applicable: takeout lens (not bio/pharma) and the deck-mark gate (no commodity linkage).

COTY.thesis_summary: Coty is a levered, licence-dependent beauty stub running a voluntary strategic review of Consumer Beauty (CoverGirl, Rimmel, Max Factor, Sally Hansen, plus a standalone Brazil business; ~$1.6bn of the segment's $2.0bn FY26 revenue is actually in scope). Management restated in the 19 Aug 2026 FY26 release that it targets "final portfolio decisions ... by the end of CY26", but on the call Strobel downgraded that to a "very strong aspiration" and said he would extend it if waiting produced a better result; the FY27 outlook explicitly does not contemplate completion. Fifteen-plus months into the process there is still no counterparty, no price and no signed agreement — SEC EDGAR carries no 8-K after 20 Aug 2026 (the CFO appointment). The one genuinely contracted item is the Gucci Beauty licence hand-back to Kering (7 Jul 2026): $250m received at signing, a further $150m due no later than 30 Sep 2027 of which up to $30m is contingent, plus unquantified inventory proceeds, with Coty operating the brand through at least 30 Jun 2027 and a "sizable" unquantified FY28 profit step-down thereafter. Re-derived on the live FY26 segment tape the sum-of-the-parts is ~$3.80 against a ~$1.85 no-deal floor and a $2.93 last close — the good outcome pays less than the bad outcome costs.
COTY.dated_milestone: Q1 FY27 results, early November 2026 — the first SCHEDULED checkpoint on the Consumer Beauty strategic review. Management's own target ("final portfolio decisions related to our strategic review of Consumer Beauty by the end of CY26", 19 Aug 2026 FY26 release) is a soft aspiration, not a contractual date: on the Q4 call Strobel called completing it in CY26 a "very strong aspiration" and said he would wait longer if it yielded a materially better outcome, and the FY27 outlook does not contemplate completion. The only contractually binding dated items are Gucci: Coty operates the brand through at least 30 June 2027, and the remaining $150m (of which up to $30m is contingent) is due no later than 30 September 2027.
COTY.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim — that a Consumer Beauty disposal converts into ~$600m of enterprise value for shareholders — is refutable from Coty's own filings. The board impaired CB by $362.8m in FY26 while shopping it, and the division lost $43.2m at the ADJUSTED operating line on $2,000.8m of revenue with adjusted EBITDA of $67.8m (down 66% y/y, 3.4% margin); a buyer of an EBIT-negative, share-losing mass-colour portfolio pays for restructuring, not for revenue, so even the 0.30x-sales mark may be too high. The review's actual scope is only the ~$1.2bn colour-cosmetics core plus the ~$400m Brazil business (~80% of the segment), and the outcome set management describes — "partnerships, divestitures, spin-offs" — is dominated by paths that deliver NO cash, leaving $2,912.1m of financial net debt against a shrinking EBITDA base. The catalyst is management's own uncontracted calendar with no counterparty after fifteen months, the FY28 Gucci step-down lands before any disposal proceeds can compound, FY27 is self-described as a "transition year" with no FY27 guidance, and there is an open securities suit and fiduciary-duty investigation over the Consumer Beauty disclosure. Residual risk: negative asymmetry — corrected R:R is ~0.8:1 in the win case.

Soft, not hard; not SLIPPED because the stated date has not yet moved.

Financial leverage is 3.4x with no covenant event, FY26 free cash flow was +$348.2m and debt fell from $3,216.2m (Mar-26) to $3,088.2m (Jun-26). This is a voluntary portfolio review whose resolution is a transaction announcement; tagging it Forced_divest_flow would mis-bucket it against genuinely compelled sellers under the 2-per-driver cap.

This is nonetheless FIRMER than the skeptic's $1.78 because $250m of Gucci cash has now actually landed and $400m is contracted.

VERIFIED FY26 TAPE (all from the 19 Aug release): consolidated revenue $5,806.6m (-2% reported, -5% LFL); adjusted EBITDA $846.9m (-22%); reported operating LOSS $81.5m; FCF $348.2m. Prestige revenue $3,805.8m, adjusted EBITDA $779.1m (20.5%). Consumer Beauty revenue $2,000.8m (-3%, -7% LFL), adjusted EBITDA $67.8m (-66%, 3.4% margin), adjusted operating LOSS $43.2m, and $362.8m of asset-impairment charges booked in the year. Financial net debt $2,912.1m ($3,088.2m total debt less $176.1m cash), leverage 3.4x. Q1 FY27 guide: LFL down low-to-mid single digit, adjusted gross margin -50 to -100bp, adjusted EBITDA down low-teens %. No FY27 guidance.

SOP, SHOWN (the "0.5x revenue" mark is exactly the deck-price problem in another costume — a conditional cap, not fair value):
  Prestige post-Gucci EBITDA $650m (FY26 $779.1m less the ~$130m FY28 Gucci step-down; NOTE the release itself does NOT quantify this, saying only a "sizable mechanical impact", and Gucci is a "low double-digit percentage" of group revenue, so $120-140m is a call/consensus figure carrying real error bars)
  x 9.0x = $5,850m. 9.0x rather than 9.5x because Kering has just demonstrated a licensor can repossess a licence a year early, and the whole Prestige book (Burberry, Hugo Boss, Calvin Klein, Marc Jacobs, Chloe, Davidoff) is licensed.
  Consumer Beauty at 0.30x FY26 revenue $2,000.8m = $600m (= 8.9x its $67.8m EBITDA). The board's 0.50x = $1,000m = 14.7x EBITDA on an EBIT-negative asset the board impaired $362.8m while marketing it. Both numbers stated: $600m is the mark, $1,000m is the conditional cap.
  Gross EV $6,450m
  + Gucci residual, firm portion only $120m (the $150m due by 30 Sep 2027 less the up-to-$30m contingent; inventory proceeds unquantified upside; pre cash tax)
  - Financial net debt $2,912.1m (excludes a further $182.9m of finance leases)
  - Convertible Series B preferred $142.4m (23.7m conversion shares; if-converted value at $2.93 is only ~$69m, so this deduction is the conservative one)
  - separation / stranded-cost / transaction leakage $150m
  = $3,365.5m equity / 880.4m shares = $3.82 -> FAIR VALUE TARGET $3.80.
  Sensitivity: CB at 0.50x adds $400m = +$0.45/sh ($4.25); CB at 0.20x removes $200m = -$0.23 ($3.57); Prestige at 9.5x adds $325m = +$0.37.

FLOOR, SHOWN (no-deal / review concludes in "retain and fix"): FY28 run-rate adjusted EBITDA ~$650m (FY26 $846.9m, less the guided ~10% FY27 decline, less ~$130m of Gucci) x 7.0x = $4,550m EV; net debt ~$2,600m by then (the $400m Gucci cash plus ~$300m/yr of FCF applied to debt); less $142.4m preferred = $1,807m / 880.4m = $2.05. At 6.5x the same bridge gives $1.68. DOWNSIDE FLOOR $1.85, mid-band and corroborated by the actual 52-week low print of $1.82.

ASYMMETRY: from $2.93, +29.7% to $3.80 against -36.9% to $1.85 = 0.81:1. The corrected win case pays less than the bear case costs. This is a FACT about the axes, not a verdict — the CRO owns the trade.

STATUS LOGIC: catalyst_live=true (real, forward-dated, unfired, idiosyncratic). PENDING_SOFT because the resolving event is a management aspiration, not a contractual date, and because "final portfolio decisions" can resolve as "we decided to keep it" or "we decided to spin, execution FY28" — neither of which produces the cash the SoP win case requires. staging=true. Driver corrected to Deal_close_generic: this is a voluntary review by a company generating $348m of FCF and repaying debt, not a forced sale.

Not a bio/pharma name, so no takeout lens applies. One process overhang worth flagging as fact: a federal securities suit and a fiduciary-duty investigation (Kuehn Law, 27 Jul and 18 Aug 2026 releases) are open over the Consumer Beauty disclosure — that is background noise for valuation but it is live litigation the CRO should see.
